nodes.name: Coinjectivity via k = 1, so R is permutative and its disjoint union with the lit

nodes.statement: For a type index \( \beta \), a \emph{\( \beta \)-approximation} is a \( \beta \)-tree of base approximations. We define the partial order on \( \beta \)-approximations branchwise. We define an action of \( \beta \)-approximations \( \psi \) on \( \beta \)-supports \( S \) by \( (\psi(S))_A = \psi_A(S_A) \).
nodes.name: beta-approximation
nodes.label: def:StrApprox

nodes.statement: Let \( A \) be a \( \beta \)-extended type index. A litter \( L \) is \emph{\( A \)-inflexible} if there is an inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I \) such that \( A = ((A_I)_{\varepsilon_I})_\bot \) and \( L = f_{\delta_I, \varepsilon_I}(t) \) for some \( t : \Tang_{\delta_I} \). The coderivative operation works in the obvious way. A litter can be \( A \)-inflexible in at most one way.\footnote{We should make \( A \)-inflexibility into a subsingleton structure.} We say that a \( L \) is \emph{\( A \)-flexible} if it is not \( A \)-inflexible.\footnote{This is not data, but a proposition.} If \( L \) is \( B_A \)-flexible, then \( L \) is \( A \)-flexible.
nodes.name: A-inflexible litter
nodes.label: def:Inflexible

nodes.statement: A \( \beta \)-approximation \( \psi \) is \emph{coherent} at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \) if: \begin{itemize} \item If \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \), then there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \] (and hence all \( \delta \)-allowable permutations \( \rho \) such that \( (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \) satisfy \( L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \)). \item If \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-flexible, then \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-flexible. \end{itemize} We say that \( \psi \) is \emph{coherent} if whenever \( (L_1, L_2) \in \psi_A^\Litter \), \( \psi \) is coherent at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \).
nodes.name: coherent approximation
nodes.label: def:StrApprox.Coherent

nodes.statement: Suppose that \( \psi \) is an approximation and \( L : \mathbb Z \to \Litter \) is a function satisfying the hypotheses of \cref{prop:BaseApprox.addOrbit}. Let \( \chi \) be the extension produced by the structural version of this result.\footnote{We need the extension exactly as produced (as data), not an arbitrary extension satisfying the conclusion of the proposition.} If \( \psi \) is coherent, and is additionally coherent at \( (L(n), L(n+1)) \) for each integer \( n \), then \( \chi \) is coherent.
nodes.name: adding orbits coherently
assumptions: \( \psi \) is coherent, and is additionally coherent at \( (L(n), L(n+1)) \) for each integer \( n \)
conclusions: \( \chi \) is coherent
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.addOrbit

nodes.statement: This proof just relies on the fact that if \( (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \), then the same holds for every extension \( \chi \) of \( \psi \).\footnote{Maybe there's a better lemma to abstract out this idea for this and \cref{prop:StrApprox.chain}?}
nodes.name: Proof of adding orbits coherently
nodes.statement_short: Coherence witnesses persist to extensions.

nodes.statement: If \( \psi \) is coherent, then \( \psi^{-1} \) is coherent.
nodes.name: StrApprox.Coherent.inv
assumptions: \( \psi \) is coherent
conclusions: \( \psi^{-1} \) is coherent
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.Coherent.inv

nodes.statement: Suppose that \( (L_1, L_2) \in (\psi^{-1}_A)^\Litter \), so \( (L_2, L_1) \in \psi_A^\Litter \). Suppose first that \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). If \( L_2 \) were \( A \)-flexible, then \( L_1 \) would also be \( A \)-flexible by coherence, which is a contradiction. So \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma', \delta', \varepsilon', B') \) and tangle \( t' : \Tang_{\delta'} \), and there is \( \rho : \AllPerm_{\delta'} \) such that \[ (\psi_{B'})_{\delta'}(\supp(t')) = \rho(\supp(t')) \] and \[ A = (B_{\varepsilon'})_\bot;\quad L_2 = f_{\delta',\varepsilon'}(t');\quad L_1 = f_{\delta',\varepsilon'}(\rho(t')) \] We thus deduce \( \varepsilon = \varepsilon' \) and \( \gamma = \gamma' \) by the equations for \( A \). By the equation \( L_1 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), we also obtain \( \delta = \delta' \) and \( t = \rho(t') \). Then we find \begin{align*} (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^{-1}(t))) &= \rho(\supp(\rho^{-1}(t))) \\ (\psi_B)_\delta(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) &= \rho(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) \\ (\psi_B)_\delta(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) &= \supp(t) \\ \rho^{-1}(\supp(t)) &= (\psi^{-1}_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) \end{align*} where the last equation uses the fact that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t') \). Finally, the equation \( L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{-1}(t)) \) gives coherence at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \) as required. Now suppose that \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-flexible. If \( L_2 \) were \( A \)-inflexible, then so would be \( L_1 \) by coherence. So \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-flexible, as required.
nodes.name: Proof of StrApprox.Coherent.inv
nodes.statement_short: Case split on flexibility of L_1; in the inflexible case match inflexible paths and invert the witnessing permutation.
Take an edge of the inverse.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( (L_1, L_2) \in (\psi^{-1}_A)^\Litter \), so \( (L_2, L_1) \in \psi_A^\Litter \).
nodes.name: Take an edge of the inverse

nodes.statement_short: Inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Suppose first that \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). If \( L_2 \) were \( A \)-flexible, then \( L_1 \) would also be \( A \)-flexible by coherence, which is a contradiction. So \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma', \delta', \varepsilon', B') \) and tangle \( t' : \Tang_{\delta'} \), and there is \( \rho : \AllPerm_{\delta'} \) such that \[ (\psi_{B'})_{\delta'}(\supp(t')) = \rho(\supp(t')) \] and \[ A = (B_{\varepsilon'})_\bot;\quad L_2 = f_{\delta',\varepsilon'}(t');\quad L_1 = f_{\delta',\varepsilon'}(\rho(t')) \] We thus deduce \( \varepsilon = \varepsilon' \) and \( \gamma = \gamma' \) by the equations for \( A \). By the equation \( L_1 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), we also obtain \( \delta = \delta' \) and \( t = \rho(t') \). Then we find \begin{align*} (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^{-1}(t))) &= \rho(\supp(\rho^{-1}(t))) \\ (\psi_B)_\delta(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) &= \rho(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) \\ (\psi_B)_\delta(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) &= \supp(t) \\ \rho^{-1}(\supp(t)) &= (\psi^{-1}_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) \end{align*} where the last equation uses the fact that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t') \). Finally, the equation \( L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{-1}(t)) \) gives coherence at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \) as required.
nodes.name: Inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: L_2 cannot be flexible.
nodes.statement: If \( L_2 \) were \( A \)-flexible, then \( L_1 \) would also be \( A \)-flexible by coherence, which is a contradiction.
nodes.name: L_2 cannot be flexible

nodes.statement_short: Coherence of psi at (L_2, L_1) gives a witness rho.
nodes.statement: So \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma', \delta', \varepsilon', B') \) and tangle \( t' : \Tang_{\delta'} \), and there is \( \rho : \AllPerm_{\delta'} \) such that \[ (\psi_{B'})_{\delta'}(\supp(t')) = \rho(\supp(t')) \] and \[ A = (B_{\varepsilon'})_\bot;\quad L_2 = f_{\delta',\varepsilon'}(t');\quad L_1 = f_{\delta',\varepsilon'}(\rho(t')) \]
nodes.name: Coherence of psi at (L_2, L_1) gives a witness rho

nodes.statement_short: The inflexible paths and tangles match.
nodes.statement: We thus deduce \( \varepsilon = \varepsilon' \) and \( \gamma = \gamma' \) by the equations for \( A \). By the equation \( L_1 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), we also obtain \( \delta = \delta' \) and \( t = \rho(t') \).
nodes.name: The inflexible paths and tangles match

nodes.statement_short: Invert the support equation.
nodes.statement: Then we find \begin{align*} (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^{-1}(t))) &= \rho(\supp(\rho^{-1}(t))) \\ (\psi_B)_\delta(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) &= \rho(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) \\ (\psi_B)_\delta(\rho^{-1}(\supp(t))) &= \supp(t) \\ \rho^{-1}(\supp(t)) &= (\psi^{-1}_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) \end{align*} where the last equation uses the fact that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t') \).
nodes.name: Invert the support equation

nodes.statement_short: rho inverse witnesses coherence.
nodes.statement: Finally, the equation \( L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{-1}(t)) \) gives coherence at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \) as required.
nodes.name: rho inverse witnesses coherence

nodes.statement_short: Flexible case: L_2 flexible too.
nodes.statement: Now suppose that \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-flexible. If \( L_2 \) were \( A \)-inflexible, then so would be \( L_1 \) by coherence. So \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-flexible, as required.
nodes.name: Flexible case: L_2 flexible too

nodes.statement: If \( \psi \) and \( \chi \) are coherent and have equal coimages along all paths, then \( \psi \circ \chi \) is coherent.
nodes.name: StrApprox.Coherent.comp
assumptions: \( \psi \) and \( \chi \) are coherent and have equal coimages along all paths
conclusions: \( \psi \circ \chi \) is coherent
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.Coherent.comp

nodes.statement: Suppose that \( (L_1, L_3) \in ((\psi \circ \chi)_A)^\Litter \), so \( (L_1, L_2) \in \psi_A^\Litter \) and \( (L_2, L_3) \in \chi_A^\Litter \). Suppose that \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then by coherence of \( \psi \), we have \( \rho \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \] Then \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( I \) and tangle \( \rho(t) \). So by coherence of \( \chi \), we have \( \rho' \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho(t))) = \rho'(\supp(\rho(t))) \] and \[ L_3 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho'(\rho(t))) \] As \( \rho'(\supp(\rho(t))) = \rho'(\rho(\supp(t))) \), we obtain the desired coherence result. Instead, if \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-flexible, then so is \( L_2 \) by coherence of \( \psi \), and so is \( L_3 \) by coherence of \( \chi \).
nodes.name: Proof of StrApprox.Coherent.comp
nodes.statement_short: Case split on flexibility; compose the two coherence witnesses in the inflexible case.
Split a composite edge.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( (L_1, L_3) \in ((\psi \circ \chi)_A)^\Litter \), so \( (L_1, L_2) \in \psi_A^\Litter \) and \( (L_2, L_3) \in \chi_A^\Litter \).
nodes.name: Split a composite edge

nodes.statement_short: Inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then by coherence of \( \psi \), we have \( \rho \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \] Then \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( I \) and tangle \( \rho(t) \). So by coherence of \( \chi \), we have \( \rho' \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho(t))) = \rho'(\supp(\rho(t))) \] and \[ L_3 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho'(\rho(t))) \] As \( \rho'(\supp(\rho(t))) = \rho'(\rho(\supp(t))) \), we obtain the desired coherence result.
nodes.name: Inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: Witness rho from coherence of psi.
nodes.statement: Then by coherence of \( \psi \), we have \( \rho \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \]
nodes.name: Witness rho from coherence of psi

nodes.statement_short: L_2 is inflexible with tangle rho(t).
nodes.statement: Then \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( I \) and tangle \( \rho(t) \).
nodes.name: L_2 is inflexible with tangle rho(t)

nodes.statement_short: Witness rho' from coherence of chi.
nodes.statement: So by coherence of \( \chi \), we have \( \rho' \) such that \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho(t))) = \rho'(\supp(\rho(t))) \] and \[ L_3 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho'(\rho(t))) \]
nodes.name: Witness rho' from coherence of chi

nodes.statement_short: The product rho' rho witnesses coherence.
nodes.statement: As \( \rho'(\supp(\rho(t))) = \rho'(\rho(\supp(t))) \), we obtain the desired coherence result.
nodes.name: The product rho' rho witnesses coherence

nodes.statement_short: Flexible case passes through.
nodes.statement: Instead, if \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-flexible, then so is \( L_2 \) by coherence of \( \psi \), and so is \( L_3 \) by coherence of \( \chi \).
nodes.name: Flexible case passes through

nodes.statement: If \( \psi \) is a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation and \( A \) is a path \( \beta \tpath \beta' \), then \( \psi_A \) is a coherent \( \beta' \)-approximation.
nodes.name: StrApprox.Coherent.deriv
assumptions: \( \psi \) is a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation and \( A \) is a path \( \beta \tpath \beta' \)
conclusions: \( \psi_A \) is a coherent \( \beta' \)-approximation
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.Coherent.deriv

nodes.statement: Let \( (L_1, L_2) \in (\psi_A)_B^\Litter \). Suppose that \( L_1 \) is \( B \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, C) \) and \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then \( L_1 \) is \( A_B \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, A_C) \) and the same tangle \( t \). So by coherence of \( \psi \), we obtain a \( \delta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \[ (\psi_{(A_C)})_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \] This same \( \rho \) can thus be used to establish coherence of \( \psi_A \) at \( (B, L_1, L_2) \). Thus, by \cref{prop:StrApprox.Coherent.inv}, whenever \( L_2 \) is \( B \)-inflexible with path \( I \) and tangle \( t \), \( L_1 \) is also \( B \)-inflexible with path \( I \). So if \( L_1 \) is \( B \)-flexible, so is \( L_2 \), as required.
nodes.name: Proof of StrApprox.Coherent.deriv
nodes.statement_short: Transport inflexible paths along the derivative, then use inverse coherence for the flexible direction.
An inflexible litter for psi_A is inflexible for psi along A_B.
nodes.statement: Let \( (L_1, L_2) \in (\psi_A)_B^\Litter \). Suppose that \( L_1 \) is \( B \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, C) \) and \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then \( L_1 \) is \( A_B \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, A_C) \) and the same tangle \( t \).
nodes.name: An inflexible litter for psi_A is inflexible for psi along A_B

nodes.statement_short: Get the witness from coherence of psi.
nodes.statement: So by coherence of \( \psi \), we obtain a \( \delta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \[ (\psi_{(A_C)})_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \]
nodes.name: Get the witness from coherence of psi

nodes.statement_short: The same witness works for psi_A.
nodes.statement: This same \( \rho \) can thus be used to establish coherence of \( \psi_A \) at \( (B, L_1, L_2) \).
nodes.name: The same witness works for psi_A

nodes.statement_short: Inverse coherence gives the flexible condition.
nodes.statement: Thus, by \cref{prop:StrApprox.Coherent.inv}, whenever \( L_2 \) is \( B \)-inflexible with path \( I \) and tangle \( t \), \( L_1 \) is also \( B \)-inflexible with path \( I \). So if \( L_1 \) is \( B \)-flexible, so is \( L_2 \), as required.
nodes.name: Inverse coherence gives the flexible condition

nodes.statement: We say that a \( \beta \)-approximation \( \psi \) \emph{approximates} a \( \beta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) if \( \psi_A^\Litter \leq \rho_A^\Litter \) and \( \psi_A^\Atom \leq \rho_A^\Atom \) for each path \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \). If \( \psi \) approximates \( \rho \) then \( \psi^n \) approximates \( \rho^n \) for each \( n : \mathbb Z \).\footnote{We should define what it means for a base approximation to approximate a near-litter permutation, and define this in terms of that.} A \( \beta \)-approximation \( \psi \) \emph{exactly approximates} a \( \beta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) if \( \psi \) approximates \( \rho \), and in addition, if \( a \) is an atom and \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \), then \( a \notin \coim \psi_A^\Atom \) implies \( \rho(a)^\circ = \rho(a^\circ) \) and \( \rho^{-1}(a)^\circ = \rho^{-1}(a^\circ) \).
nodes.name: approximates
nodes.label: def:StrApprox.Approximates

nodes.statement: We say that \emph{freedom of action} holds at a type index \( \delta \) if every coherent \( \delta \)-approximation exactly approximates some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation.
nodes.name: freedom of action
nodes.label: def:FreedomOfAction

nodes.statement: Let \( \psi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation, and let \( L \) be \( A \)-flexible. Then there is a coherent extension \( \chi \geq \psi \) with \( L \in \coim \chi_A^\Litter \).
nodes.name: adding flexible litters
assumptions: Let \( \psi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation, and let \( L \) be \( A \)-flexible.
conclusions: there is a coherent extension \( \chi \geq \psi \) with \( L \in \coim \chi_A^\Litter \)
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.addFlexible

nodes.statement: Define \( L' : \mathbb Z \to \Litter \) by \( L'(n) = L \), then appeal to \cref{prop:StrApprox.addOrbit} to obtain \( \chi \geq \psi \). All we must do is check that \( \psi \) is coherent at \( (L, L) \), which is trivial.
nodes.name: Proof of adding flexible litters
nodes.statement_short: Add the constant orbit of L via adding orbits coherently; coherence at (L, L) is trivial.

nodes.statement: Let \( \psi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation, and let \( L \) be \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Suppose that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \).\footnote{This is a nontrivial definition to make.} Suppose that freedom of action holds at level \( \delta \). Then there is a coherent extension \( \chi \geq \psi \) with \( L \in \coim \chi_A^\Litter \).
nodes.name: adding inflexible litters
assumptions: Let \( \psi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation, and let \( L \) be \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \).
Suppose that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \).
Suppose that freedom of action holds at level \( \delta \).
conclusions: there is a coherent extension \( \chi \geq \psi \) with \( L \in \coim \chi_A^\Litter \)
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.addInflexible

nodes.statement: Let \( \rho \) be a \( \delta \)-allowable permutation that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) approximates. Then for each \( n : \mathbb Z \), as \( (\psi^n_B)_\delta \) approximates \( \rho^n \), we obtain \( (\psi^n_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho^n(\supp(t)) \) as \( (\psi^n_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \).\footnote{This should of course be its own lemma.} Define \( L : \mathbb Z \to \Litter \) by \( L(n) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t)) \). Suppose that there is some \( n \) such that \( L(n) \in \coim \psi^\Litter \). Note that \begin{align*} (\psi^n_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) &= \rho^n(\supp(t)) \\ \supp(t) &= (\psi^{-n}_B)_\delta(\rho^n(\supp(t))) \\ \rho^{-n}(\rho^n(\supp(t))) &= (\psi^{-n}_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) \end{align*} So as \( \psi^{-n} \) is coherent, we obtain \( (L(n), f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) \in (\psi^{-n}_A)^\Litter \). In particular, \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \in \coim \psi_A^\Litter \) already, and no work needs to be done. We first check the hypothesis of \cref{prop:BaseApprox.addOrbit} for adding orbits. If \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^m(t)) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t)) \), then \( \rho^m(t) = \rho^n(t) \), so \( \rho^{m+k}(t) = \rho^{n+k}(t) \), giving \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{m+k}(t)) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{n+k}(t)) \) as required. We now check the criterion of \cref{prop:StrApprox.addOrbit} for adding orbits coherently. It suffices to show that \( \psi \) is coherent at \( (L(n), L(n+1)) \) for each \( n : \mathbb Z \). This is witnessed by \( \rho \), which satisfies \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) = \rho(\supp(\rho^n(t))) \] and \[ L(n) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t));\quad L(n+1) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(\rho^n(t))) \] as required.\footnote{It might be helpful to abstract away the lemma \( (\psi^m_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) = \supp(\rho^{n+m}(t)) \) for the two places in the proof where this idea is used.}
nodes.name: Proof of adding inflexible litters
nodes.statement_short: Use freedom of action at delta to get rho, add the orbit of fuzz images of rho^n(t), checking the orbit hypotheses.
Take rho approximated by (psi_B)_delta, and its powers.
nodes.statement: Let \( \rho \) be a \( \delta \)-allowable permutation that \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) approximates. Then for each \( n : \mathbb Z \), as \( (\psi^n_B)_\delta \) approximates \( \rho^n \), we obtain \( (\psi^n_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho^n(\supp(t)) \) as \( (\psi^n_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \).\footnote{This should of course be its own lemma.}
nodes.name: Take rho approximated by (psi_B)_delta, and its powers

nodes.statement_short: Define the orbit L(n); if it already meets the coimage, nothing to do.
nodes.statement: Define \( L : \mathbb Z \to \Litter \) by \( L(n) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t)) \). Suppose that there is some \( n \) such that \( L(n) \in \coim \psi^\Litter \). Note that \begin{align*} (\psi^n_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) &= \rho^n(\supp(t)) \\ \supp(t) &= (\psi^{-n}_B)_\delta(\rho^n(\supp(t))) \\ \rho^{-n}(\rho^n(\supp(t))) &= (\psi^{-n}_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) \end{align*} So as \( \psi^{-n} \) is coherent, we obtain \( (L(n), f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) \in (\psi^{-n}_A)^\Litter \). In particular, \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \in \coim \psi_A^\Litter \) already, and no work needs to be done.
nodes.name: Define the orbit L(n); if it already meets the coimage, nothing to do

nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the support equation for psi^{-n}.
nodes.statement: Note that \begin{align*} (\psi^n_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) &= \rho^n(\supp(t)) \\ \supp(t) &= (\psi^{-n}_B)_\delta(\rho^n(\supp(t))) \\ \rho^{-n}(\rho^n(\supp(t))) &= (\psi^{-n}_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) \end{align*}
nodes.name: Rewrite the support equation for psi^{-n}

nodes.statement_short: Coherence links L(n) to the fuzz image of t.
nodes.statement: So as \( \psi^{-n} \) is coherent, we obtain \( (L(n), f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) \in (\psi^{-n}_A)^\Litter \).
nodes.name: Coherence links L(n) to the fuzz image of t

nodes.statement_short: L is already in the coimage.
nodes.statement: In particular, \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \in \coim \psi_A^\Litter \) already, and no work needs to be done.
nodes.name: L is already in the coimage

nodes.statement_short: Check the shift hypothesis of adding orbits.
nodes.statement: We first check the hypothesis of \cref{prop:BaseApprox.addOrbit} for adding orbits. If \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^m(t)) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t)) \), then \( \rho^m(t) = \rho^n(t) \), so \( \rho^{m+k}(t) = \rho^{n+k}(t) \), giving \( f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{m+k}(t)) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^{n+k}(t)) \) as required.
nodes.name: Check the shift hypothesis of adding orbits

nodes.statement_short: Check the coherence criterion.
nodes.statement: We now check the criterion of \cref{prop:StrApprox.addOrbit} for adding orbits coherently. It suffices to show that \( \psi \) is coherent at \( (L(n), L(n+1)) \) for each \( n : \mathbb Z \). This is witnessed by \( \rho \), which satisfies \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) = \rho(\supp(\rho^n(t))) \] and \[ L(n) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t));\quad L(n+1) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(\rho^n(t))) \] as required.\footnote{It might be helpful to abstract away the lemma \( (\psi^m_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) = \supp(\rho^{n+m}(t)) \) for the two places in the proof where this idea is used.}
nodes.name: Check the coherence criterion

nodes.statement_short: Reduce to coherence at consecutive pairs.
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that \( \psi \) is coherent at \( (L(n), L(n+1)) \) for each \( n : \mathbb Z \).
nodes.name: Reduce to coherence at consecutive pairs

nodes.statement_short: rho witnesses each step.
nodes.statement: This is witnessed by \( \rho \), which satisfies \[ (\psi_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) = \rho(\supp(\rho^n(t))) \] and \[ L(n) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho^n(t));\quad L(n+1) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(\rho^n(t))) \] as required.\footnote{It might be helpful to abstract away the lemma \( (\psi^m_B)_\delta(\supp(\rho^n(t))) = \supp(\rho^{n+m}(t)) \) for the two places in the proof where this idea is used.}
nodes.name: rho witnesses each step

nodes.statement: If \( (\psi_i)_{i : I} \) is a chain of coherent approximations where \( I \) is a linear order, then the supremum \( \psi \) is coherent.
nodes.name: StrApprox.chain
assumptions: \( (\psi_i)_{i : I} \) is a chain of coherent approximations where \( I \) is a linear order
conclusions: the supremum \( \psi \) is coherent
nodes.label: prop:StrApprox.chain

nodes.statement: Direct, using the same idea as the proof of \cref{prop:StrApprox.addOrbit}.
nodes.name: Proof of StrApprox.chain
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as adding orbits coherently.

nodes.statement: Freedom of action holds at all type indices \( \beta \leq \alpha \).
nodes.name: freedom of action
nodes.statement_short: Every coherent approximation exactly approximates an allowable permutation, at all levels up to alpha.
conclusions: Freedom of action holds at all type indices \( \beta \leq \alpha \).
nodes.label: thm:StrApprox.foa

nodes.statement: By induction, we may assume freedom of action holds at all \( \delta < \beta \). Let \( \psi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation, and let \( \chi \) be a maximal coherent extension, which exists by Zorn's lemma and \cref{prop:StrApprox.chain}. Suppose that there is a litter \( L \) such that there exists a path \( A \) where \( L \notin \coim \chi_A^\Litter \). Let \( L \) have minimal position with this property, and let \( A \) be such a path. Suppose that \( L \) is \( A \)-flexible. Then by \cref{prop:StrApprox.addFlexible}, there is an extension \( \varphi \) of \( \chi \) such that \( L \in \coim \varphi_A^\Litter \), contradicting maximality of \( \chi \). Suppose that \( L \) is \( A \)-inflexible, with path \( (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t \). Then \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \). Indeed, by \cref{def:CoherentData} (coherent data) and \cref{prop:fuzz} (fuzz maps), for each atom or near-litter \( y \) that appears in the range of \( \supp(t)_C \), we have \( \iota(y) < \iota(t) < \iota(L) \), giving the desired conclusion by minimality of the position of \( L \) and the criteria of \cref{prop:BasePositions}. Thus, we obtain the same contradiction by \cref{prop:StrApprox.addInflexible}. So \( \coim \chi_A^\Litter \) is the set of all litters for each path \( A \). We then use the fact that our model data is coherent to recursively compute the allowable permutation \( \rho \) with the same action as \( \chi \). Then \( \chi \) exactly approximates \( \rho \), so \( \psi \) also exactly approximates \( \rho \).\footnote{In general, if \( \psi \leq \chi \) and \( \chi \) (exactly) approximates \( \rho \) then \( \psi \) (exactly) approximates \( \rho \).}
nodes.name: Proof of freedom of action
nodes.statement_short: Induction on beta, Zorn's lemma for a maximal coherent extension, then a minimal-position missing litter gives a contradiction in both flexible and inflexible cases.
Assume freedom of action below beta.
nodes.statement: By induction, we may assume freedom of action holds at all \( \delta < \beta \).
nodes.name: Assume freedom of action below beta

nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal coherent extension by Zorn.
nodes.statement: Let \( \psi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-approximation, and let \( \chi \) be a maximal coherent extension, which exists by Zorn's lemma and \cref{prop:StrApprox.chain}.
nodes.name: Take a maximal coherent extension by Zorn

nodes.statement_short: Pick a missing litter of minimal position.
nodes.statement: Suppose that there is a litter \( L \) such that there exists a path \( A \) where \( L \notin \coim \chi_A^\Litter \). Let \( L \) have minimal position with this property, and let \( A \) be such a path.
nodes.name: Pick a missing litter of minimal position

nodes.statement_short: Flexible: adding flexible litters contradicts maximality.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( L \) is \( A \)-flexible. Then by \cref{prop:StrApprox.addFlexible}, there is an extension \( \varphi \) of \( \chi \) such that \( L \in \coim \varphi_A^\Litter \), contradicting maximality of \( \chi \).
nodes.name: Flexible: adding flexible litters contradicts maximality

nodes.statement_short: Inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( L \) is \( A \)-inflexible, with path \( (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t \). Then \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \). Indeed, by \cref{def:CoherentData} (coherent data) and \cref{prop:fuzz} (fuzz maps), for each atom or near-litter \( y \) that appears in the range of \( \supp(t)_C \), we have \( \iota(y) < \iota(t) < \iota(L) \), giving the desired conclusion by minimality of the position of \( L \) and the criteria of \cref{prop:BasePositions}. Thus, we obtain the same contradiction by \cref{prop:StrApprox.addInflexible}.
nodes.name: Inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: By minimality of position, the approximation is defined on supp(t).
nodes.statement: Then \( (\psi_B)_\delta \) is defined on all of \( \supp(t) \). Indeed, by \cref{def:CoherentData} (coherent data) and \cref{prop:fuzz} (fuzz maps), for each atom or near-litter \( y \) that appears in the range of \( \supp(t)_C \), we have \( \iota(y) < \iota(t) < \iota(L) \), giving the desired conclusion by minimality of the position of \( L \) and the criteria of \cref{prop:BasePositions}.
nodes.name: By minimality of position, the approximation is defined on supp(t)

nodes.statement_short: Adding inflexible litters contradicts maximality.
nodes.statement: Thus, we obtain the same contradiction by \cref{prop:StrApprox.addInflexible}.
nodes.name: Adding inflexible litters contradicts maximality

nodes.statement_short: Every litter is in the coimage.
nodes.statement: So \( \coim \chi_A^\Litter \) is the set of all litters for each path \( A \).
nodes.name: Every litter is in the coimage

nodes.statement_short: Build rho from coherent data; chi and so psi exactly approximate it.
nodes.statement: We then use the fact that our model data is coherent to recursively compute the allowable permutation \( \rho \) with the same action as \( \chi \). Then \( \chi \) exactly approximates \( \rho \), so \( \psi \) also exactly approximates \( \rho \).\footnote{In general, if \( \psi \leq \chi \) and \( \chi \) (exactly) approximates \( \rho \) then \( \psi \) (exactly) approximates \( \rho \).}
nodes.name: Build rho from coherent data; chi and so psi exactly approximate it

nodes.statement: The \emph{interference} of near-litters \( N_1, N_2 \) is \[ \interf(N_1, N_2) = \begin{cases} N_1 \symmdiff N_2 & \text{if } N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \\ N_1 \cap N_2 & \text{if } N_1^\circ \neq N_2^\circ \end{cases} \] which is a small set of atoms.
nodes.name: interference
nodes.label: def:Interference

nodes.statement: A \emph{base action} is a pair \( \xi = (\xi^\Atom, \xi^\NearLitter) \) such that \( \xi^\Atom \) and \( \xi^\NearLitter \) are relations of atoms and near-litters respectively (\cref{def:relation_props}), such that \begin{itemize} \item \( \xi^\Atom \) and \( \xi^\NearLitter \) are defined on small sets; \item \( \xi^\Atom \) is one-to-one; \item if \( (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \); \item if \( (N_1, N_3), (N_2, N_4) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \) if and only if \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \); \item for each \( (N_1, N_3), (N_2, N_4) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), \[ \interf(N_1, N_2) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom;\quad \interf(N_3, N_4) \subseteq \im \xi^\Atom \] \end{itemize} Note that these conditions imply that \( \xi^\NearLitter \) is one-to-one. We define the one-to-one relation \( \xi^\Litter \) by the constructor \[ (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \to (N_1^\circ, N_2^\circ) \in \xi^\Litter \] The partial order on base actions is defined by \( \xi \leq \zeta \) if and only if \( \xi^\Atom \leq \zeta^\Atom \) and \( \xi^\NearLitter = \zeta^\NearLitter \).\footnote{We should make utilities for constructing extensions of base actions, reducing the proof obligations of showing that these are base actions (e.g.\ removing the last two bullet points and not needing to prove results we already know about \( \xi \)).} The inverse of \( \xi \) is \( ((\xi^\Atom)^{-1}, (\xi^\NearLitter)^{-1}) \). They act on base supports in the natural way.
nodes.name: base action
nodes.statement_short: A base action is a pair of small one-to-one relations on atoms and near-litters compatible with membership, litters and interference.
nodes.label: def:BaseAction

nodes.statement: A base action \( \xi \) is \emph{nice} if whenever \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), \[ N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom;\quad N_2 \symmdiff \LS(N_2^\circ) \subseteq \im \xi^\Atom \]
nodes.name: nice base action
nodes.label: def:BaseAction.Nice

nodes.statement: Every base action \( \xi \) admits an extension \( \zeta \) satisfying \[ \forall N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter,\, N \setminus \LS(N^\circ) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \]
nodes.name: extending orbits inside near-litters
conclusions: Every base action \( \xi \) admits an extension \( \zeta \) satisfying \[ \forall N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter,\, N \setminus \LS(N^\circ) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \]
nodes.label: prop:BaseAction.exists_inside

nodes.statement:
For each litter \( L \), there is an injection \[ i_L :  igcup_{N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter} (N \setminus \LS(N^\circ)) 	o \{ a : \Atom \mid a^\circ = L \wedge  orall N \in \im \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = L 	o a \in N \} \setminus \im \xi^\Atom \] by a cardinality argument. Define the relation \( R \) on atoms by the constructor \[  orall (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter,\,  orall a \in N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom,\, (a, i_{N_2^\circ}(a)) \in R \] This is one-to-one and has disjoint image and coimage from \( \xi^\Atom \). We now show that if \( (a_1, a_2) \in R \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \). Let \( (N_1, N_2), (N_1', N_2') \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( a \in N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom \). Suppose that \( a \in N_1' \); we must show \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \). If \( N_1^\circ 
eq {N_1'}^\circ \), then \( \interf(N_1, N_1') = N_1 \cap N_1' \), so \( a \in \interf(N_1, N_1') \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction. So \( N_1^\circ = {N_1'}^\circ \), giving \( N_2^\circ = {N_2'}^\circ \), so \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) = i_{{N_2'}^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \) by definition. Conversely, suppose that \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \); we must show \( a \in N_1' \). Note that by definition, \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2 \). So if \( N_2^\circ 
eq {N_2'}^\circ \), we would have \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2 \cap N_2' = \interf(N_2, N_2') \subseteq \im \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction. Hence \( N_2^\circ = {N_2'}^\circ \) and \( N_1^\circ = {N_1'}^\circ \). Thus, if \( a 
otin N_1' \), we would have \( a \in N_1 \symmdiff N_1' = \interf(N_1, N_1') \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), again a contradiction. Hence \( \zeta = (\xi^\Atom \sqcup R, \xi^\NearLitter) \) is a base action and satisfies the conclusion.
nodes.name: Proof of extending orbits inside near-litters
nodes.statement_short: Map the extra atoms of each near-litter injectively into the target litter by a cardinality argument and check the base-action conditions via interference.
Injections into the target litters exist by cardinality.
nodes.statement: For each litter \( L \), there is an injection \[ i_L : \bigcup_{N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter} (N \setminus \LS(N^\circ)) \to \{ a : \Atom \mid a^\circ = L \wedge \forall N \in \im \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = L \to a \in N \} \setminus \im \xi^\Atom \] by a cardinality argument.
nodes.name: Injections into the target litters exist by cardinality

nodes.statement_short: Define the new atom relation R.
nodes.statement: Define the relation \( R \) on atoms by the constructor \[ \forall (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter,\, \forall a \in N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom,\, (a, i_{N_2^\circ}(a)) \in R \] This is one-to-one and has disjoint image and coimage from \( \xi^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Define the new atom relation R

nodes.statement_short: Forward direction of the membership condition.
nodes.statement: We now show that if \( (a_1, a_2) \in R \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \). Let \( (N_1, N_2), (N_1', N_2') \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( a \in N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom \). Suppose that \( a \in N_1' \); we must show \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \). If \( N_1^\circ \neq {N_1'}^\circ \), then \( \interf(N_1, N_1') = N_1 \cap N_1' \), so \( a \in \interf(N_1, N_1') \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction. So \( N_1^\circ = {N_1'}^\circ \), giving \( N_2^\circ = {N_2'}^\circ \), so \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) = i_{{N_2'}^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \) by definition.
nodes.name: Forward direction of the membership condition

nodes.statement_short: Fix near-litters and an atom a.
nodes.statement: Let \( (N_1, N_2), (N_1', N_2') \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( a \in N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom \). Suppose that \( a \in N_1' \); we must show \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \).
nodes.name: Fix near-litters and an atom a

nodes.statement_short: Different litters would put a in the interference.
nodes.statement: If \( N_1^\circ \neq {N_1'}^\circ \), then \( \interf(N_1, N_1') = N_1 \cap N_1' \), so \( a \in \interf(N_1, N_1') \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction.
nodes.name: Different litters would put a in the interference

nodes.statement_short: Equal litters give the image in N_2'.
nodes.statement: So \( N_1^\circ = {N_1'}^\circ \), giving \( N_2^\circ = {N_2'}^\circ \), so \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) = i_{{N_2'}^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \) by definition.
nodes.name: Equal litters give the image in N_2'

nodes.statement_short: Converse direction.
nodes.statement: Conversely, suppose that \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2' \); we must show \( a \in N_1' \). Note that by definition, \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2 \). So if \( N_2^\circ \neq {N_2'}^\circ \), we would have \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2 \cap N_2' = \interf(N_2, N_2') \subseteq \im \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction. Hence \( N_2^\circ = {N_2'}^\circ \) and \( N_1^\circ = {N_1'}^\circ \). Thus, if \( a \notin N_1' \), we would have \( a \in N_1 \symmdiff N_1' = \interf(N_1, N_1') \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), again a contradiction.
nodes.name: Converse direction

nodes.statement_short: The image lies in N_2.
nodes.statement: Note that by definition, \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2 \).
nodes.name: The image lies in N_2

nodes.statement_short: Different litters contradict interference; so litters agree.
nodes.statement: So if \( N_2^\circ \neq {N_2'}^\circ \), we would have \( i_{N_2^\circ}(a) \in N_2 \cap N_2' = \interf(N_2, N_2') \subseteq \im \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction. Hence \( N_2^\circ = {N_2'}^\circ \) and \( N_1^\circ = {N_1'}^\circ \).
nodes.name: Different litters contradict interference; so litters agree

nodes.statement_short: a in N_1' else interference contradiction.
nodes.statement: Thus, if \( a \notin N_1' \), we would have \( a \in N_1 \symmdiff N_1' = \interf(N_1, N_1') \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), again a contradiction.
nodes.name: a in N_1' else interference contradiction

nodes.statement_short: The extension is a base action.
nodes.statement: Hence \( \zeta = (\xi^\Atom \sqcup R, \xi^\NearLitter) \) is a base action and satisfies the conclusion.
nodes.name: The extension is a base action

nodes.statement: Every base action \( \xi \) admits an extension \( \zeta \) satisfying \[ \forall N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter,\, \LS(N) \setminus N \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \]
nodes.name: extending orbits outside near-litters
conclusions: Every base action \( \xi \) admits an extension \( \zeta \) satisfying \[ \forall N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter,\, \LS(N) \setminus N \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \]
nodes.label: prop:BaseAction.exists_outside

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality (as extensions are transitive), let \( \xi \) satisfy the conclusion of \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside}. Let \( L \) be an arbitrary litter that whose litter set does not contain an atom in \( \im \xi^\Atom \) or \( \bigcup \im \xi^\NearLitter \). Define an injection \[ i : \bigcup_{N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter} (\LS(N^\circ) \setminus N \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom) \to \LS(L) \] by a cardinality argument. Note that \( i \) has domain disjoint from \( \coim \xi^\Atom \) and image disjoint from \( \im \xi^\Atom \). We show that \( (\xi^\Atom \sqcup \graph i, \xi^\NearLitter) \) is a base action. It suffices to check that if \( (a_1, a_2) \in \graph i \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \). As \( a_2 \in \LS(L) \), we have \( a_2 \notin N_2 \). Suppose that \( a_1 \in N_1 \). We know that there is a near-litter \( N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter \) such that \( a_1 \in \LS(N^\circ) \setminus N \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom \). If \( N^\circ = N_1^\circ \), then \( a_1 \in N \symmdiff N_1 = \interf(N, N_1) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction, hence \( a^\circ = N^\circ \neq N_1^\circ \). But then as \( \xi \) satisfies the conclusion of \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside}, we have \( N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), which again is a contradiction.
nodes.name: Proof of extending orbits outside near-litters
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the inside case, inject the missing litter atoms into a fresh litter, and check the membership condition via interference.
WLOG the inside conclusion holds.
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality (as extensions are transitive), let \( \xi \) satisfy the conclusion of \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside}.
nodes.name: WLOG the inside conclusion holds

nodes.statement_short: Choose a fresh litter and an injection into it.
nodes.statement: Let \( L \) be an arbitrary litter that whose litter set does not contain an atom in \( \im \xi^\Atom \) or \( \bigcup \im \xi^\NearLitter \). Define an injection \[ i : \bigcup_{N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter} (\LS(N^\circ) \setminus N \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom) \to \LS(L) \] by a cardinality argument.
nodes.name: Choose a fresh litter and an injection into it

nodes.statement_short: Domain and image are disjoint from xi.
nodes.statement: Note that \( i \) has domain disjoint from \( \coim \xi^\Atom \) and image disjoint from \( \im \xi^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Domain and image are disjoint from xi

nodes.statement_short: The extension is a base action.
nodes.statement: We show that \( (\xi^\Atom \sqcup \graph i, \xi^\NearLitter) \) is a base action. It suffices to check that if \( (a_1, a_2) \in \graph i \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \). As \( a_2 \in \LS(L) \), we have \( a_2 \notin N_2 \). Suppose that \( a_1 \in N_1 \). We know that there is a near-litter \( N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter \) such that \( a_1 \in \LS(N^\circ) \setminus N \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom \). If \( N^\circ = N_1^\circ \), then \( a_1 \in N \symmdiff N_1 = \interf(N, N_1) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction, hence \( a^\circ = N^\circ \neq N_1^\circ \). But then as \( \xi \) satisfies the conclusion of \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside}, we have \( N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), which again is a contradiction.
nodes.name: The extension is a base action

nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the membership condition.
nodes.statement: It suffices to check that if \( (a_1, a_2) \in \graph i \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \).
nodes.name: Reduce to the membership condition

nodes.statement_short: The new image atom is outside N_2.
nodes.statement: As \( a_2 \in \LS(L) \), we have \( a_2 \notin N_2 \).
nodes.name: The new image atom is outside N_2

nodes.statement_short: Assume a_1 in N_1 and take its source near-litter N.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( a_1 \in N_1 \). We know that there is a near-litter \( N \in \coim \xi^\NearLitter \) such that \( a_1 \in \LS(N^\circ) \setminus N \setminus \coim \xi^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Assume a_1 in N_1 and take its source near-litter N

nodes.statement_short: Same litter puts a_1 in the interference, so litters differ.
nodes.statement: If \( N^\circ = N_1^\circ \), then \( a_1 \in N \symmdiff N_1 = \interf(N, N_1) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), a contradiction, hence \( a^\circ = N^\circ \neq N_1^\circ \).
nodes.name: Same litter puts a_1 in the interference, so litters differ

nodes.statement_short: The inside property gives a contradiction.
nodes.statement: But then as \( \xi \) satisfies the conclusion of \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside}, we have \( N_1 \setminus \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \xi^\Atom \), which again is a contradiction.
nodes.name: The inside property gives a contradiction

nodes.statement: Every base action has a nice extension.
nodes.name: BaseAction.exists_nice
conclusions: Every base action has a nice extension.
nodes.label: prop:BaseAction.exists_nice

nodes.statement: Apply \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside} to \( \xi \) to obtain \( \xi_1 \); apply \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_inside} again to \( \xi_1^{-1} \) to obtain \( \xi_2 \); apply \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_outside} to \( \xi_2 \) to obtain \( \xi_3 \), and finally apply \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_outside} again to \( \xi_3^{-1} \) to obtain \( \xi_4 \), our target.
nodes.name: Proof of BaseAction.exists_nice
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inside and outside extension results to xi and inverses in turn.

nodes.statement: For a type index \( \beta \), a \emph{\( \beta \)-action} is a \( \beta \)-tree of base actions. We define an action of \( \beta \)-actions \( \xi \) on \( \beta \)-supports \( S \) by \( (\xi(S))_A = \xi_A(S_A) \).
nodes.name: beta-action
nodes.label: def:StrAction

nodes.statement: A \( \beta \)-action \( \xi \) is \emph{coherent} at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \) if: \begin{itemize} \item If \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma, \delta, \varepsilon, B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \), then there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \[ (\xi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \] and \[ L_2 = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \] (and hence again every \( \delta \)-allowable \( \rho \) satisfying the hypothesis also satisfies the conclusion). \item If \( L_1 \) is \( A \)-flexible, then \( L_2 \) is \( A \)-flexible. \end{itemize} We say that \( \xi \) is \emph{coherent} if whenever \( (L_1, L_2) \in \xi_A^\Litter \), \( \xi \) is coherent at \( (A, L_1, L_2) \).
nodes.name: coherent action
nodes.label: def:StrAction.Coherent

nodes.statement: Let \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \). An \emph{\( A \)-flexible approximation} of a base action \( \xi \) is a base approximation \( \psi \) such that \begin{enumerate} \item \( \xi^\Atom \leq \psi^{E\Atom} \); \item if \( L \in \coim \psi^\Litter \), then \( L \) is \( A \)-flexible; \item if \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \) and \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, then \( (N_1^\circ, N_2^\circ) \in \psi^\Litter \); \item if \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then \( N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \psi^\Atom \) and \( N_2 \symmdiff \LS(N_2^\circ) \subseteq \coim \psi^\Atom \); \item if \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), then for each atom \( a_2 \), \[ a_2 \in N_2 \leftrightarrow (\exists a_1 \in N_1,\, (a_1, a_2) \in \psi^{E\Atom}) \vee (a_2 \notin \coim \psi^{E\Atom} \wedge a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ) \] \end{enumerate} A \emph{flexible approximation} of a \( \beta \)-action \( \xi \) is a \( \beta \)-approximation \( \psi \) such that for each \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \), the base approximation \( \psi_A \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation of \( \xi_A \). Flexible approximations are coherent.
nodes.name: flexible approximation
nodes.statement_short: An A-flexible approximation of a base action extends its atoms and its flexible litters consistently with near-litter membership.
nodes.label: def:FlexApprox

nodes.statement: Every base action has an \( A \)-flexible approximation. Hence, every \( \beta \)-action has a flexible approximation, which can be computed branchwise.
nodes.name: exists_flexApprox
conclusions: Every base action has an \( A \)-flexible approximation.
every \( \beta \)-action has a flexible approximation, which can be computed branchwise
nodes.label: prop:exists_flexApprox

nodes.statement:
If \( \xi \leq \zeta \) and \( \psi \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation for \( \zeta \), then \( \psi \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation for \( \xi \). So it suffices to prove the result for nice base actions \( \xi \) by \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_nice}. Define the permutative relation \( R : \Litter 	o \Litter 	o \Prop \) to be a permutative extension of \( \xi^\Litter \), which exists by \cref{prop:completing_orbits}. Let \( \pi \) be the permutation of litters defined by \( R \), or the identity on any litter not in \( \coim R \). Define an orbit restriction \( (t, f, \pi) \) (\cref{def:OrbitRestriction}) for \(  ield \xi^\Atom \) by \[ u = \{ a : \Atom \mid  orall N \in  ield \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = a^\circ 	o a \in N \};\quad t = u \setminus  ield \xi^\Atom \] with function \( f : \Atom 	o \Litter \) defined by \( f(a) = a^\circ \), and litter permutation \( \pi \). We must check that for each litter \( L \), the set \( t \cap \LS(L) \) has cardinality at least \( \max(\aleph_0, \# ield \xi^\Atom) \). But we can write \[ t \cap \LS(L) = \LS(L) \setminus \left(  ield \xi^\Atom \cup  igcup_{N \in  ield \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = L} (\LS(L) \setminus N) ight) \] where the set being removed from \( \LS(L) \) is small, so \( t \cap \LS(L) \) is a large set, and \( \aleph_0 \) and \( \# ield \xi^\Atom \) are less than \( \#\kappa \), as required. Then by \cref{prop:completing_restricted_orbits}, there is a permutative relation \( S \geq \xi^\Atom \) defined on a small set and contained in \(  ield \xi^\Atom \cup t =  ield \xi^\Atom \cup u \), such that if \[ (a_1, a_2) \in S 	o (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \vee \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ \] Let \( T \) be a permutative extension of the restriction of \( \xi^\Litter \) to the \( A \)-flexible litters, with coimage contained entirely in the set of \( A \)-flexible litters, given by \cref{prop:completing_orbits}. From this, we define a base approximation \( \psi = (S, T) \). It remains to check that \( \psi \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation of \( \xi \). Conditions 1--3 are trivial, and condition 4 follows from the fact that we assumed \( \xi \) was nice. We first show an auxiliary result. Let \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \); we will show that \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_2 \in N_2 \). Suppose first that \( (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \), in which case we are done as \( \xi \) is a base action. Instead, we have \( a_1 
otin \coim \xi^\Atom, a_2 
otin \im \xi^\Atom \) and \( \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ \). As \( \xi \) is nice, we must have \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_1^\circ = N_1^\circ \). Similarly, \( a_2 \in N_2 \leftrightarrow a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \). So if \( a_1 \in N_1 \), we conclude that \( a_2^\circ = \pi(a_1^\circ) = \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \) giving \( a_2 \in N_2 \), and if \( a_2 \in N_2 \), we find \( \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \) so \( a_1^\circ = N_1^\circ \), giving \( a_1 \in N_1 \). We now prove condition 5, which is the equation \[ a_2 \in N_2 \leftrightarrow (\exists a_1 \in N_1,\, (a_1, a_2) \in S) \vee (a_2 
otin \coim S \wedge a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ) \] where \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \). Consider the first the case where \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \) and \( a_1 \in N_1 \). The auxiliary lemma shows that \( a_2 \in N_2 \) as required. Now consider the case where \( a_2

otin N_1) \wedge (a_2 \in \coim S \vee a_2^\circ 
eq N_2^\circ) \] If \( a_2 \in \coim S \), then there is \( a_1 \) such that \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \), and we have \( a_1

nodes.name: Proof of exists_flexApprox
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to nice actions, complete the litter orbits and the restricted atom orbits, and verify the five flexible-approximation conditions. The key step is an auxiliary lemma relating membership through the new atom pairs.
Reduce to nice base actions.
nodes.statement: If \( \xi \leq \zeta \) and \( \psi \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation for \( \zeta \), then \( \psi \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation for \( \xi \). So it suffices to prove the result for nice base actions \( \xi \) by \cref{prop:BaseAction.exists_nice}.
nodes.name: Reduce to nice base actions

nodes.statement_short: Complete the litter orbits to a permutation pi.
nodes.statement: Define the permutative relation \( R : \Litter \to \Litter \to \Prop \) to be a permutative extension of \( \xi^\Litter \), which exists by \cref{prop:completing_orbits}. Let \( \pi \) be the permutation of litters defined by \( R \), or the identity on any litter not in \( \coim R \).
nodes.name: Complete the litter orbits to a permutation pi

nodes.statement_short: Complete the atom orbits under an orbit restriction.
nodes.statement: Define an orbit restriction \( (t, f, \pi) \) (\cref{def:OrbitRestriction}) for \( \field \xi^\Atom \) by \[ u = \{ a : \Atom \mid \forall N \in \field \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = a^\circ \to a \in N \};\quad t = u \setminus \field \xi^\Atom \] with function \( f : \Atom \to \Litter \) defined by \( f(a) = a^\circ \), and litter permutation \( \pi \). We must check that for each litter \( L \), the set \( t \cap \LS(L) \) has cardinality at least \( \max(\aleph_0, \#\field \xi^\Atom) \). But we can write \[ t \cap \LS(L) = \LS(L) \setminus \left( \field \xi^\Atom \cup \bigcup_{N \in \field \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = L} (\LS(L) \setminus N) \right) \] where the set being removed from \( \LS(L) \) is small, so \( t \cap \LS(L) \) is a large set, and \( \aleph_0 \) and \( \#\field \xi^\Atom \) are less than \( \#\kappa \), as required. Then by \cref{prop:completing_restricted_orbits}, there is a permutative relation \( S \geq \xi^\Atom \) defined on a small set and contained in \( \field \xi^\Atom \cup t = \field \xi^\Atom \cup u \), such that if \[ (a_1, a_2) \in S \to (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \vee \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ \]
nodes.name: Complete the atom orbits under an orbit restriction

nodes.statement_short: Define the sandbox t and categorisation.
nodes.statement: Define an orbit restriction \( (t, f, \pi) \) (\cref{def:OrbitRestriction}) for \( \field \xi^\Atom \) by \[ u = \{ a : \Atom \mid \forall N \in \field \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = a^\circ \to a \in N \};\quad t = u \setminus \field \xi^\Atom \] with function \( f : \Atom \to \Litter \) defined by \( f(a) = a^\circ \), and litter permutation \( \pi \).
nodes.name: Define the sandbox t and categorisation

nodes.statement_short: The sandbox is large in each litter.
nodes.statement: We must check that for each litter \( L \), the set \( t \cap \LS(L) \) has cardinality at least \( \max(\aleph_0, \#\field \xi^\Atom) \). But we can write \[ t \cap \LS(L) = \LS(L) \setminus \left( \field \xi^\Atom \cup \bigcup_{N \in \field \xi^\NearLitter,\, N^\circ = L} (\LS(L) \setminus N) \right) \] where the set being removed from \( \LS(L) \) is small, so \( t \cap \LS(L) \) is a large set, and \( \aleph_0 \) and \( \#\field \xi^\Atom \) are less than \( \#\kappa \), as required.
nodes.name: The sandbox is large in each litter

nodes.statement_short: Complete restricted orbits to get S.
nodes.statement: Then by \cref{prop:completing_restricted_orbits}, there is a permutative relation \( S \geq \xi^\Atom \) defined on a small set and contained in \( \field \xi^\Atom \cup t = \field \xi^\Atom \cup u \), such that if \[ (a_1, a_2) \in S \to (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \vee \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ \]
nodes.name: Complete restricted orbits to get S

nodes.statement_short: Complete flexible litter orbits to T and set psi = (S, T).
nodes.statement: Let \( T \) be a permutative extension of the restriction of \( \xi^\Litter \) to the \( A \)-flexible litters, with coimage contained entirely in the set of \( A \)-flexible litters, given by \cref{prop:completing_orbits}. From this, we define a base approximation \( \psi = (S, T) \).
nodes.name: Complete flexible litter orbits to T and set psi = (S, T)

nodes.statement_short: Conditions 1-4 are immediate or from niceness.
nodes.statement: It remains to check that \( \psi \) is an \( A \)-flexible approximation of \( \xi \). Conditions 1--3 are trivial, and condition 4 follows from the fact that we assumed \( \xi \) was nice.
nodes.name: Conditions 1-4 are immediate or from niceness

nodes.statement: We first show an auxiliary result. Let \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \); we will show that \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_2 \in N_2 \). Suppose first that \( (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \), in which case we are done as \( \xi \) is a base action. Instead, we have \( a_1 \notin \coim \xi^\Atom, a_2 \notin \im \xi^\Atom \) and \( \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ \). As \( \xi \) is nice, we must have \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_1^\circ = N_1^\circ \). Similarly, \( a_2 \in N_2 \leftrightarrow a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \). So if \( a_1 \in N_1 \), we conclude that \( a_2^\circ = \pi(a_1^\circ) = \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \) giving \( a_2 \in N_2 \), and if \( a_2 \in N_2 \), we find \( \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \) so \( a_1^\circ = N_1^\circ \), giving \( a_1 \in N_1 \).
nodes.name: auxiliary result (membership through S)
assumptions: Let \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \)
conclusions: \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_2 \in N_2 \)

nodes.statement_short: Fix a near-litter pair and an atom pair.
nodes.statement: Let \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \), and let \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \); we will show that \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_2 \in N_2 \).
nodes.name: Fix a near-litter pair and an atom pair

nodes.statement_short: Old pairs: xi is a base action.
nodes.statement: Suppose first that \( (a_1, a_2) \in \xi^\Atom \), in which case we are done as \( \xi \) is a base action.
nodes.name: Old pairs: xi is a base action

nodes.statement_short: New pairs: membership reduces to litters by niceness.
nodes.statement: Instead, we have \( a_1 \notin \coim \xi^\Atom, a_2 \notin \im \xi^\Atom \) and \( \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ \). As \( \xi \) is nice, we must have \( a_1 \in N_1 \leftrightarrow a_1^\circ = N_1^\circ \). Similarly, \( a_2 \in N_2 \leftrightarrow a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \).
nodes.name: New pairs: membership reduces to litters by niceness

nodes.statement_short: Litter permutation pi transfers membership both ways.
nodes.statement: So if \( a_1 \in N_1 \), we conclude that \( a_2^\circ = \pi(a_1^\circ) = \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \) giving \( a_2 \in N_2 \), and if \( a_2 \in N_2 \), we find \( \pi(a_1^\circ) = a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \) so \( a_1^\circ = N_1^\circ \), giving \( a_1 \in N_1 \).
nodes.name: Litter permutation pi transfers membership both ways

nodes.statement_short: Prove condition 5.

We now prove condition 5, which is the equation \[ a_2 \in N_2 \leftrightarrow (\exists a_1 \in N_1,\, (a_1, a_2) \in S) \vee (a_2 
otin \coim S \wedge a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ) \] where \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \). Consider the first the case where \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \) and \( a_1 \in N_1 \). The auxiliary lemma shows that \( a_2 \in N_2 \) as required. Now consider the case where \( a_2 
otin \coim S \) and \( a_2^\circ = N_2^\circ \). If \( a_2

eq N_2^\circ) \] If \( a_2 \in \coim S \), then there is \( a_1 \) such that \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \), and we have \( a_1

nodes.statement_short: Image case via the auxiliary lemma.

otin N_1) \wedge (a_2 \in \coim S \vee a_2^\circ

otin N_1 \), giving \( a_2 
otin N_2 \) by the auxiliary lemma. Finally, if \( a_2

otin N_2 \), since \( a_2 \in N_2 \) would imply \( a_2 \in N_2 \symmdiff \LS(N_2^\circ) \), contradicting the fact that \( \xi \) is nice.
nodes.name: Neither case: a_2 not in N_2

nodes.statement_short: Via the auxiliary lemma.
nodes.statement: If \( a_2 \in \coim S \), then there is \( a_1 \) such that \( (a_1, a_2) \in S \), and we have \( a_1 \notin N_1 \), giving \( a_2 \notin N_2 \) by the auxiliary lemma.

Finally, if \( a_2 
otin \coim S \) and \( a_2^\circ 
eq N_2^\circ \), then \( a_2
