nodes.statement: We say that a \( \beta \)-action \( \xi \) \emph{approximates} a \( \beta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) if \( \xi_A^\NearLitter \leq \rho_A^\NearLitter \) and \( \xi_A^\Atom \leq \rho_A^\Atom \) for each path \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \).\footnote{Again, we should define what it means for a base action to approximate a near-litter permutation, and define this in terms of that.}
nodes.name: approximates
nodes.label: def:StrAction.Approximates

nodes.statement: Let \( \xi \) be a base action, and let \( \psi \) be an \( A \)-flexible approximation of it. Let \( \pi \) be a base permutation that \( \psi \) exactly approximates. If \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \) and \( \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \), then \( \pi(N_1) = N_2 \).
nodes.name: FlexApprox.smul_nearLitter_eq
assumptions: Let \( \xi \) be a base action, and let \( \psi \) be an \( A \)-flexible approximation of it.
Let \( \pi \) be a base permutation that \( \psi \) exactly approximates.
\( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi^\NearLitter \) and \( \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \)
nodes.label: prop:FlexApprox.smul_nearLitter_eq

nodes.statement: First, note that \begin{align*} \pi[N_1] &= \pi[\LS(N_1^\circ)] \symmdiff \pi[N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)] \\ &= (\pi[\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}] \cup \pi[\LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}]) \symmdiff \pi[N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)] \end{align*} As \( \psi \) exactly approximates \( \pi \) and \( \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \), we have the equation \[ \pi[\LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}] = \LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom} \] Combining this with the fact that \( \psi^{E\Atom} \leq \pi^\Atom \), and that \( N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \psi^{E\Atom} \), we obtain \begin{align*} \pi[N_1] &= (\im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}} \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom})) \symmdiff \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)} \\ &= (\im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}} \symmdiff \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)}) \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \\ &= \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{(\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \symmdiff (N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ))} \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \\ &= \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{N_1 \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}} \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \end{align*} which is equal to \( N_2 \) by part of \cref{def:FlexApprox}.
nodes.name: Proof of FlexApprox.smul_nearLitter_eq
nodes.statement_short: Decompose pi[N_1] into its litter part and exceptional part and compute using exact approximation.
Split pi[N_1] by the litter set and the exceptional coimage.
nodes.statement: First, note that \begin{align*} \pi[N_1] &= \pi[\LS(N_1^\circ)] \symmdiff \pi[N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)] \\ &= (\pi[\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}] \cup \pi[\LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}]) \symmdiff \pi[N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)] \end{align*}
nodes.name: Split pi[N_1] by the litter set and the exceptional coimage

nodes.statement_short: Exact approximation fixes the non-exceptional part.
nodes.statement: As \( \psi \) exactly approximates \( \pi \) and \( \pi(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \), we have the equation \[ \pi[\LS(N_1^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}] = \LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom} \]
nodes.name: Exact approximation fixes the non-exceptional part

nodes.statement_short: Compute pi[N_1] and match the flexible approximation condition.
nodes.statement: Combining this with the fact that \( \psi^{E\Atom} \leq \pi^\Atom \), and that \( N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ) \subseteq \coim \psi^{E\Atom} \), we obtain \begin{align*} \pi[N_1] &= (\im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}} \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom})) \symmdiff \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)} \\ &= (\im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}} \symmdiff \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ)}) \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \\ &= \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{(\LS(N_1^\circ) \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \symmdiff (N_1 \symmdiff \LS(N_1^\circ))} \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \\ &= \im \psi^{E\Atom}|_{N_1 \cap \coim \psi^{E\Atom}} \cup (\LS(N_2^\circ) \setminus \coim \psi^{E\Atom}) \end{align*} which is equal to \( N_2 \) by part of \cref{def:FlexApprox}.
nodes.name: Compute pi[N_1] and match the flexible approximation condition

nodes.statement: Let \( \xi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-action, and let \( \psi \) be a flexible approximation for it. If \( \psi \) exactly approximates some allowable permutation \( \rho \), then \( \xi \) approximates \( \rho \).
nodes.name: approximates_of_flexApprox
assumptions: Let \( \xi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-action, and let \( \psi \) be a flexible approximation for it.
\( \psi \) exactly approximates some allowable permutation \( \rho \)
conclusions: \( \xi \) approximates \( \rho \)
nodes.label: prop:approximates_of_flexApprox

nodes.statement: First, note that \( \xi_A^\Atom \leq \psi_A^{E\Atom} \) and \( \psi_A^\Atom \leq \rho_A^\Atom \) give the required result for atoms. Now suppose that \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi_A^\NearLitter \); we must show that \( \rho_A(N_1) = N_2 \). We prove this by induction on \( \iota(N_1) \), generalising over all \( A \). By \cref{prop:FlexApprox.smul_nearLitter_eq}, it suffices to show that \( \rho_A(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \). Suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible. Then by \cref{def:FlexApprox}, \( (N_1^\circ, N_2^\circ) \in \psi_A^\Litter \). Hence \( \rho_A(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \) as required. Suppose not, so \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). By coherence of \( \xi \), we know that \( (\xi_B)_\delta \) is defined on \( \supp(t) \), and it suffices to show that \[ (\xi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = (\rho_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) \] Let \( C : \delta \tpath \bot \) and \( a \) be an atom such that \( (i, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom \) for some \( i \). Then \( (a, ((\rho_B)_\delta)_C(a)) \in ((\xi_B)_\delta)_C^\Atom \) by the result for atoms. Now suppose \( N \) is a near-litter such that \( (i, N) \in \supp(t)_C^\NearLitter \). Then \[ \iota(N) < \iota(t) < \iota(f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) = \iota(N_1^\circ) \] So we may apply the inductive hypothesis, giving \( (N, ((\rho_B)_\delta)_C(N)) \in ((\xi_B)_\delta)_C^\NearLitter \) as required.
nodes.name: Proof of approximates_of_flexApprox
nodes.statement_short: Atoms are immediate; near-litters by induction on position, with a flexible/inflexible case split using coherence.
The atom part is immediate.
nodes.statement: First, note that \( \xi_A^\Atom \leq \psi_A^{E\Atom} \) and \( \psi_A^\Atom \leq \rho_A^\Atom \) give the required result for atoms.
nodes.name: The atom part is immediate

nodes.statement_short: Induct on iota(N_1) for near-litters.
nodes.statement: Now suppose that \( (N_1, N_2) \in \xi_A^\NearLitter \); we must show that \( \rho_A(N_1) = N_2 \). We prove this by induction on \( \iota(N_1) \), generalising over all \( A \).
nodes.name: Induct on iota(N_1) for near-litters

nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the litter images.
nodes.statement: By \cref{prop:FlexApprox.smul_nearLitter_eq}, it suffices to show that \( \rho_A(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \).
nodes.name: Reduce to the litter images

nodes.statement_short: Flexible: the litter edge lies in psi.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible. Then by \cref{def:FlexApprox}, \( (N_1^\circ, N_2^\circ) \in \psi_A^\Litter \). Hence \( \rho_A(N_1^\circ) = N_2^\circ \) as required.
nodes.name: Flexible: the litter edge lies in psi

nodes.statement_short: Inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Suppose not, so \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-inflexible with path \( (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). By coherence of \( \xi \), we know that \( (\xi_B)_\delta \) is defined on \( \supp(t) \), and it suffices to show that \[ (\xi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = (\rho_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) \] Let \( C : \delta \tpath \bot \) and \( a \) be an atom such that \( (i, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom \) for some \( i \). Then \( (a, ((\rho_B)_\delta)_C(a)) \in ((\xi_B)_\delta)_C^\Atom \) by the result for atoms. Now suppose \( N \) is a near-litter such that \( (i, N) \in \supp(t)_C^\NearLitter \). Then \[ \iota(N) < \iota(t) < \iota(f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) = \iota(N_1^\circ) \] So we may apply the inductive hypothesis, giving \( (N, ((\rho_B)_\delta)_C(N)) \in ((\xi_B)_\delta)_C^\NearLitter \) as required.
nodes.name: Inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: Reduce to agreement on supp(t).
nodes.statement: By coherence of \( \xi \), we know that \( (\xi_B)_\delta \) is defined on \( \supp(t) \), and it suffices to show that \[ (\xi_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = (\rho_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) \]
nodes.name: Reduce to agreement on supp(t)

nodes.statement_short: Atoms of supp(t) agree.
nodes.statement: Let \( C : \delta \tpath \bot \) and \( a \) be an atom such that \( (i, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom \) for some \( i \). Then \( (a, ((\rho_B)_\delta)_C(a)) \in ((\xi_B)_\delta)_C^\Atom \) by the result for atoms.
nodes.name: Atoms of supp(t) agree

nodes.statement_short: Near-litters of supp(t) have smaller position; apply the induction hypothesis.
nodes.statement: Now suppose \( N \) is a near-litter such that \( (i, N) \in \supp(t)_C^\NearLitter \). Then \[ \iota(N) < \iota(t) < \iota(f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) = \iota(N_1^\circ) \] So we may apply the inductive hypothesis, giving \( (N, ((\rho_B)_\delta)_C(N)) \in ((\xi_B)_\delta)_C^\NearLitter \) as required.
nodes.name: Near-litters of supp(t) have smaller position; apply the induction hypothesis

nodes.statement: Every coherent action approximates some allowable permutation.
nodes.name: freedom of action for actions
nodes.statement_short: Every coherent structural action approximates some allowable permutation.
conclusions: Every coherent action approximates some allowable permutation.
nodes.label: thm:StrAction.foa

nodes.statement: Let \( \xi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-action, and let \( \psi \) be a flexible approximation for it, which exists by \cref{prop:exists_flexApprox}. Then apply \cref{thm:StrApprox.foa} (freedom of action) to \( \psi \) to obtain a \( \beta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) that \( \psi \) exactly approximates. Finally, appeal to \cref{prop:approximates_of_flexApprox} to conclude that \( \xi \) approximates \( \rho \).
nodes.name: Proof of freedom of action for actions
nodes.statement_short: Take a flexible approximation, apply freedom of action, and transfer back.
Take a flexible approximation.
nodes.statement: Let \( \xi \) be a coherent \( \beta \)-action, and let \( \psi \) be a flexible approximation for it, which exists by \cref{prop:exists_flexApprox}.
nodes.name: Take a flexible approximation

nodes.statement_short: Freedom of action gives rho.
nodes.statement: Then apply \cref{thm:StrApprox.foa} (freedom of action) to \( \psi \) to obtain a \( \beta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) that \( \psi \) exactly approximates.
nodes.name: Freedom of action gives rho

nodes.statement_short: xi approximates rho.
nodes.statement: Finally, appeal to \cref{prop:approximates_of_flexApprox} to conclude that \( \xi \) approximates \( \rho \).
nodes.name: xi approximates rho

nodes.statement: We define a preorder \( \preceq \) on base supports by \( S \preceq T \) if and only if \( \im S^\Atom \subseteq \im T^\Atom \) and \( \im S^\NearLitter \subseteq \im T^\NearLitter \). For \( \beta \)-supports, we define \( S \preceq T \) if and only if \( S_A \preceq T_A \) for each \( A \).
nodes.name: support preorder
nodes.label: def:StrSupport.Occurs

nodes.statement: A \( \beta \)-support \( S \) is \emph{strong} if: \begin{itemize} \item for every pair of near-litters \( N_1, N_2 \in \im S_A^\NearLitter \), we have \( \interf(N_1, N_2) \subseteq \im S_A^\Atom \); and \item for every inflexible path \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,A) \) and \( t : \Tang_\delta \), if there is a near-litter \( N \in \im S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) with \( N^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), then \( \supp(t) \preceq S_{A_\delta} \). \end{itemize}
nodes.name: strong support
nodes.label: def:Strong

nodes.statement: If \( S \) is a strong \( \beta \)-support and \( \rho \) is \( \beta \)-allowable, then \( \rho(S) \) is strong.
nodes.name: Strong.smul
assumptions: \( S \) is a strong \( \beta \)-support and \( \rho \) is \( \beta \)-allowable
conclusions: \( \rho(S) \) is strong
nodes.label: prop:Strong.smul

nodes.statement: Interference is stable under application of allowable permutations, and the required supports are also preserved under action of allowable permutations.
nodes.name: Proof of Strong.smul
nodes.statement_short: Interference and the required supports are invariant under allowable permutations.

nodes.statement: For every support \( S \), there is a strong support \( T \succeq S \).
nodes.name: exists_strong
conclusions: For every support \( S \), there is a strong support \( T \succeq S \).
nodes.label: prop:exists_strong

nodes.statement: We define a relation \( R \) on pairs \( (A, N) \) where \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \) and \( N \) is a near-litter by the following constructor. If \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,A) \) and \( t : \Tang_\delta \), then for any near-litter \( N_1 \) such that \( N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \) and any path \( B : \delta \tpath \bot \) and near-litter \( N_2 \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter \), we define \( ((A_\delta)_B, N_2) \mathrel{R} ((A_\varepsilon)_\bot, N_1) \). This is well-founded, because if \( (B, N_2) \mathrel{R} (A, N_1) \) then \( \iota(N_2) < \iota(N_1) \). For any small set \( s \) of such pairs, the transitive closure of \( s \) under \( R \) is small. Let \( S \) be a support, and let \( s \) be the transitive closure of the set of pairs \( (A, N) \) such that \( N \in \im S_A^\NearLitter \). Generate a support \( T \) from \( S \) and \( s \) using the fact that every small set is the range of some enumeration. This satisfies the second condition of being a strong support. Now, for any base support \( T \), we define its \emph{interference support} to be a base support \( U \) consisting of just the atoms in the interference of all near-litters that appear in \( T \). We may extend this definition to structural supports. Finally, if \( U \) is the interference support of the \( T \) defined above, the support \( T + U \) is strong, and since \( S \succeq T \), we conclude \( S \preceq T + U \).
nodes.name: Proof of exists_strong
nodes.statement_short: Close the support under the well-founded inflexible-dependency relation, then add its interference support.
Define the dependency relation R.
nodes.statement: We define a relation \( R \) on pairs \( (A, N) \) where \( A : \beta \tpath \bot \) and \( N \) is a near-litter by the following constructor. If \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,A) \) and \( t : \Tang_\delta \), then for any near-litter \( N_1 \) such that \( N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \) and any path \( B : \delta \tpath \bot \) and near-litter \( N_2 \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter \), we define \( ((A_\delta)_B, N_2) \mathrel{R} ((A_\varepsilon)_\bot, N_1) \).
nodes.name: Define the dependency relation R

nodes.statement_short: R is well-founded and small sets have small closures.
nodes.statement: This is well-founded, because if \( (B, N_2) \mathrel{R} (A, N_1) \) then \( \iota(N_2) < \iota(N_1) \). For any small set \( s \) of such pairs, the transitive closure of \( s \) under \( R \) is small.
nodes.name: R is well-founded and small sets have small closures

nodes.statement_short: Generate T from S and its closure.
nodes.statement: Let \( S \) be a support, and let \( s \) be the transitive closure of the set of pairs \( (A, N) \) such that \( N \in \im S_A^\NearLitter \). Generate a support \( T \) from \( S \) and \( s \) using the fact that every small set is the range of some enumeration. This satisfies the second condition of being a strong support.
nodes.name: Generate T from S and its closure

nodes.statement_short: Define the interference support.
nodes.statement: Now, for any base support \( T \), we define its \emph{interference support} to be a base support \( U \) consisting of just the atoms in the interference of all near-litters that appear in \( T \). We may extend this definition to structural supports.
nodes.name: Define the interference support

nodes.statement_short: T + U is strong and extends S.
nodes.statement: Finally, if \( U \) is the interference support of the \( T \) defined above, the support \( T + U \) is strong, and since \( S \succeq T \), we conclude \( S \preceq T + U \).
nodes.name: T + U is strong and extends S

nodes.statement: For a type index \( \beta \leq \alpha \), a \emph{\( \beta \)-support orbit} is the quotient of \( \StrSupp_\beta \) under the relation of being in the same orbit under \( \beta \)-allowable permutations.\footnote{This can be implemented using \texttt{MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient}. We need to make sure there's plenty of API for support orbits to avoid code duplication.}
nodes.name: support orbit
nodes.label: def:SupportOrbit

nodes.statement: For any type index \( \beta \leq \alpha \), a \emph{\( \beta \)-coding function} is a relation \( \chi : \StrSupp_\beta \to \TSet_\beta \to \Prop \) such that: \begin{itemize} \item \( \chi \) is coinjective; \item \( \chi \) is nonempty; \item if \( (S, x) \in \chi \), then \( S \) is a support for \( x \); \item if \( S, T \in \coim \chi \) then \( S \) and \( T \) are in the same support orbit; \item if \( (S, x) \in \chi \) and \( \rho \) is \( \beta \)-allowable, then \( (\rho(S), \rho(x)) \in \chi \). \end{itemize}
nodes.name: coding function
nodes.label: def:CodingFunction

nodes.statement: Let \( \chi_1, \chi_2 \) be \( \beta \)-coding functions. If \( (S, x) \in \chi_1, \chi_2 \), then \( \chi_1 = \chi_2 \).
nodes.name: extensionality for coding functions
assumptions: Let \( \chi_1, \chi_2 \) be \( \beta \)-coding functions.
\( (S, x) \in \chi_1, \chi_2 \)
nodes.label: prop:CodingFunction.ext

nodes.statement: We show \( \chi_1 \subseteq \chi_2 \); the result then follows by antisymmetry. Suppose \( (T, y) \in \chi_1 \). Then \( T = \rho(S) \) for some \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \). As \( (\rho(S), \rho(x)) \in \chi_1 \) and \( \chi_1 \) is coinjective, we obtain \( y = \rho(x) \). Hence \( (T, y) \in \chi_2 \) as required.
nodes.name: Proof of extensionality for coding functions
nodes.statement_short: Show one inclusion via the support orbit and coinjectivity; conclude by antisymmetry.
Reduce to one inclusion.
nodes.statement: We show \( \chi_1 \subseteq \chi_2 \); the result then follows by antisymmetry.
nodes.name: Reduce to one inclusion

nodes.statement_short: Write T = rho(S).
nodes.statement: Suppose \( (T, y) \in \chi_1 \). Then \( T = \rho(S) \) for some \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \).
nodes.name: Write T = rho(S)

nodes.statement_short: Coinjectivity gives y = rho(x).
nodes.statement: As \( (\rho(S), \rho(x)) \in \chi_1 \) and \( \chi_1 \) is coinjective, we obtain \( y = \rho(x) \). Hence \( (T, y) \in \chi_2 \) as required.
nodes.name: Coinjectivity gives y = rho(x)

nodes.statement: Let \( t : \Tang_\beta \). Then we define the coding function \( \chi_t \) by the constructor \[ \forall \rho : \AllPerm_\beta,\, (\rho(\supp(t)), \rho(\set(t))) \in \chi \] This is clearly a coding function, and satisfies \( (\supp(t), \set(t)) \in \chi_t \).
nodes.name: coding function of a tangle
nodes.label: def:code

nodes.statement: Let \( t, u : \Tang_\beta \). Then \( \chi_t = \chi_u \) if and only if there is a \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \) with \( \rho(t) = u \).
nodes.name: code_eq_code_iff
assumptions: Let \( t, u : \Tang_\beta \).
conclusions: \( \chi_t = \chi_u \) if and only if there is a \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \) with \( \rho(t) = u \)
nodes.label: def:code_eq_code_iff

nodes.statement: If \( \rho(t) = u \), then \( (\supp(t), \set(t)) \in \chi_t \) implies \( (\supp(u), \set(u)) \in \chi_t \), giving \( \chi_t = \chi_u \) by \cref{prop:CodingFunction.ext}. Conversely if \( \chi_t = \chi_u \), then \( (\supp(u), \set(u)) \in \chi_t \), so there is \( \rho \) such that \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \supp(u) \), and \( (\rho(\supp(t)), \rho(\set(t))) \in \chi_t \), so by coinjectivity we obtain \( \rho(set(t)) = \set(u) \) as required.
nodes.name: Proof of code_eq_code_iff
nodes.statement_short: Both directions via extensionality of coding functions and coinjectivity.

nodes.statement: An \emph{atom condition} is a pair \( (s, t) \) where \( s, t : \Set \kappa \). A \emph{\( \beta \)-near-litter condition} is either \begin{itemize} \item a \emph{flexible condition}, consisting of a set \( s : \Set \kappa \); or \item an \emph{inflexible condition}, consisting of an inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,A) \), a \( \delta \)-coding function \( \chi \), and two \( \delta \)-trees \( R^\Atom, R^\NearLitter \) of relations on \( \kappa \). \end{itemize} A \emph{\( \beta \)-specification} is a pair \( (\sigma^\Atom, \sigma^\NearLitter) \) where \begin{itemize} \item \( \sigma^\Atom \) is a \( \beta \)-tree of enumerations of atom conditions; and \item \( \sigma^\NearLitter \) is a \( \beta \)-tree of enumerations of \( \beta \)-near-litter conditions. \end{itemize}
nodes.name: specification
nodes.label: def:Spec

nodes.statement: Let \( S \) be a \( \beta \)-support. Then \emph{its specification} is the \( \beta \)-specification \( \sigma = \spec(S) \) given by the following constructors. \begin{itemize} \item Whenever \( (i, a) \in S_A^\Atom \), we have \( (i, (s, t)) \in \sigma_A^\Atom \) where \[ s = \{ j : \kappa \mid (j, a) \in S_A^\Atom \};\quad t = \{ j : \kappa \mid \exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a \in N \} \] \item Whenever \( (i, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, we have \( (i, c) \in \sigma_A^\NearLitter \) where \( c \) is the flexible condition given by \[ s = \{ j : \kappa \mid \exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N^\circ = {N'}^\circ \} \] \item Whenever \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,A) \) is an inflexible \( \beta \)-path, \( t : \Tang_\delta \), and \( (i, N) \in S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) is such that \( N^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), we have \( (i, c) \in \sigma_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) where \( c \) is the inflexible condition given by path \( I \) and coding function \( \chi_t \), and \( R^\Atom \) and \( R^\NearLitter \) are the \( \delta \)-trees of relations given by the constructors \begin{align*} &\forall i,\, \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \to (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \to (i, j) \in R_B^\Atom \\ &\forall i,\, \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \to (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter \to (i, j) \in R_B^\NearLitter \end{align*} \end{itemize}
nodes.name: specification of a support
nodes.statement_short: The specification of a support records, for each entry, index sets of related entries and, for inflexible litters, coding data.
nodes.label: def:StrSupport.spec

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be \( \beta \)-supports. Then \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \) if and only if\footnote{The following bullet points should comprise a proposition type relating \( S \) and \( T \).} \begin{itemize} \item \( \coim S_A^\Atom = \coim T_A^\Atom \) and \( \coim S_A^\NearLitter = \coim T_A^\NearLitter \). \item (atom condition) Whenever \( (i, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \] and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_1 \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_2 \in N) \] \item (flexible condition) Whenever \( (i, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \), if \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, then so is \( N_2^\circ \), and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_1^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_2^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] \item (inflexible condition) Let \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon) \) be an inflexible \( \beta \)-path and let \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then whenever \( (i, N_1) \in S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) are such that \( N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( N_2^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \), and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} \end{itemize}
nodes.name: spec_eq_spec_iff
nodes.statement_short: Two supports have the same specification iff coimages, atom, flexible and inflexible conditions agree.
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be \( \beta \)-supports.
conclusions: \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \) if and only if\footnote{The following bullet points should comprise a proposition type relating \( S \) and \( T \).} \begin{itemize} \item \( \coim S_A^\Atom = \coim T_A^\Atom \) and \( \coim S_A^\NearLitter = \coim T_A^\NearLitter \). \item (atom condition) Whenever \( (i, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \] and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_1 \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_2 \in N) \] \item (flexible condition) Whenever \( (i, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \), if \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, then so is \( N_2^\circ \), and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_1^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_2^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] \item (inflexible condition) Let \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon) \) be an inflexible \( \beta \)-path and let \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then whenever \( (i, N_1) \in S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) are such that \( N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( N_2^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \), and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} \end{itemize}
equivalent_conditions: \begin{itemize} \item \( \coim S_A^\Atom = \coim T_A^\Atom \) and \( \coim S_A^\NearLitter = \coim T_A^\NearLitter \). \item (atom condition) Whenever \( (i, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \] and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_1 \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_2 \in N) \] \item (flexible condition) Whenever \( (i, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \), if \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, then so is \( N_2^\circ \), and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_1^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_2^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] \item (inflexible condition) Let \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon) \) be an inflexible \( \beta \)-path and let \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Then whenever \( (i, N_1) \in S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) are such that \( N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \), there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( N_2^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \), and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} \end{itemize}
nodes.label: prop:spec_eq_spec_iff

nodes.statement: We will only sketch the fourth bullet point of this proof; the remainder is direct (but quite long to write down on paper). Moreover, we will show this for atoms; the result for near-litters is identical. The specifications \( \spec(S) \) and \( \spec(T) \) give rise to the same trees \( R^\Atom \) precisely when \[ \forall i,\, \forall j,\, (\exists a,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \wedge (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom) \leftrightarrow (\exists a,\, (i, a) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \wedge (j, a) \in \supp(\rho(t))_B^\Atom) \] We must show that this holds if and only if \[ \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \] This can be concluded by appealing to the basic behaviour of \( \rho \) and noting the coinjectivity of \( \supp(t)_B^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Proof of spec_eq_spec_iff
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: unfold when the inflexible relation trees agree and compare with the permutation condition using coinjectivity.
Only the inflexible condition for atoms is sketched.
nodes.statement: We will only sketch the fourth bullet point of this proof; the remainder is direct (but quite long to write down on paper). Moreover, we will show this for atoms; the result for near-litters is identical.
nodes.name: Only the inflexible condition for atoms is sketched

nodes.statement_short: When the R-trees agree.
nodes.statement: The specifications \( \spec(S) \) and \( \spec(T) \) give rise to the same trees \( R^\Atom \) precisely when \[ \forall i,\, \forall j,\, (\exists a,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \wedge (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom) \leftrightarrow (\exists a,\, (i, a) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \wedge (j, a) \in \supp(\rho(t))_B^\Atom) \]
nodes.name: When the R-trees agree

nodes.statement_short: Target equivalence.
nodes.statement: We must show that this holds if and only if \[ \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \]
nodes.name: Target equivalence

nodes.statement_short: Conclude from coinjectivity of supp(t).
nodes.statement: This can be concluded by appealing to the basic behaviour of \( \rho \) and noting the coinjectivity of \( \supp(t)_B^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Conclude from coinjectivity of supp(t)

nodes.statement: Let \( \rho \) be \( \beta \)-allowable, and let \( S \) be a \( \beta \)-support. Then \( \spec(\rho(S)) = \spec(S) \).
nodes.name: spec_smul
assumptions: Let \( \rho \) be \( \beta \)-allowable, and let \( S \) be a \( \beta \)-support.
conclusions: \( \spec(\rho(S)) = \spec(S) \)
nodes.label: prop:spec_smul

nodes.statement: We appeal to \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}. Clearly the coimage condition holds. For the atom condition, we must check that if \( (i, a) \in S_A^\Atom \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (j, a) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, \rho_A(a)) \in \rho(S)_A^\Atom \] and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in \rho(S)_A^\NearLitter \wedge \rho_A(a) \in N) \] both of which are trivial. For the flexible condition, we must check that if \( (i, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, then \( \rho_A(N)^\circ \) is also \( A \)-flexible (which is direct, and should already be its own lemma), and that \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in \rho(S)_A^\NearLitter \wedge \rho(N)^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] which is similarly trivial. Finally, for the inflexible condition, suppose that \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon) \) is an inflexible \( \beta \)-path and \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Let \( (i, N) \in S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) be such that \( N^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \). Then by the coherence condition, \[ \rho_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}(N)^\circ = \rho_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}(N^\circ) = \rho_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}(f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho_{A_\delta}(t)) \] We must check that \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, (\rho_{A_\delta})_B(a)) \in \rho(S)_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, (\rho_{A_\delta})_B(N)) \in \rho(S)_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} which again is trivial.
nodes.name: Proof of spec_smul
nodes.statement_short: Check each condition of spec_eq_spec_iff for rho(S); all trivial except the inflexible one, which uses the coherence of fuzz maps.
Use the characterisation; coimages agree.
nodes.statement: We appeal to \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}. Clearly the coimage condition holds.
nodes.name: Use the characterisation; coimages agree

nodes.statement_short: Atom condition is trivial.
nodes.statement: For the atom condition, we must check that if \( (i, a) \in S_A^\Atom \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (j, a) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, \rho_A(a)) \in \rho(S)_A^\Atom \] and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in \rho(S)_A^\NearLitter \wedge \rho_A(a) \in N) \] both of which are trivial.
nodes.name: Atom condition is trivial

nodes.statement_short: Flexible condition is trivial.
nodes.statement: For the flexible condition, we must check that if \( (i, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible, then \( \rho_A(N)^\circ \) is also \( A \)-flexible (which is direct, and should already be its own lemma), and that \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in \rho(S)_A^\NearLitter \wedge \rho(N)^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] which is similarly trivial.
nodes.name: Flexible condition is trivial

nodes.statement_short: Set up the inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Finally, for the inflexible condition, suppose that \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon) \) is an inflexible \( \beta \)-path and \( t : \Tang_\delta \). Let \( (i, N) \in S_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}^\NearLitter \) be such that \( N^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \).
nodes.name: Set up the inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: Coherence moves rho through the fuzz map.
nodes.statement: Then by the coherence condition, \[ \rho_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}(N)^\circ = \rho_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}(N^\circ) = \rho_{{A_\varepsilon}_\bot}(f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t)) = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho_{A_\delta}(t)) \]
nodes.name: Coherence moves rho through the fuzz map

nodes.statement_short: The remaining conditions are trivial.
nodes.statement: We must check that \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, (\rho_{A_\delta})_B(a)) \in \rho(S)_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, (\rho_{A_\delta})_B(N)) \in \rho(S)_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} which again is trivial.
nodes.name: The remaining conditions are trivial

nodes.statement: Let \( S \) and \( T \) be base supports. We define the relations \( \conv_{S,T}^\Atom, \conv_{S,T}^\NearLitter \) by the constructors\footnote{This should be abstracted out even further; this can be defined for any pair of relations with common domain.} \begin{align*} &(i, a_1) \in S^\Atom \to (i, a_2) \in T^\Atom \to (a_1, a_2) \in \conv_{S,T}^\Atom \\ &(i, N_1) \in S^\NearLitter \to (i, N_2) \in T^\NearLitter \to (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S,T}^\NearLitter \end{align*} Note that \( {\conv_{S,T}^\Atom}^{-1} = \conv_{T,S}^\Atom \) and \( {\conv_{S,T}^\NearLitter}^{-1} = \conv_{T,S}^\NearLitter \).
nodes.name: conversion relations
nodes.label: def:conv_base

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). Then \( \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) is one-to-one.
nodes.name: conv_one_to_one
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \).
conclusions: \( \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) is one-to-one
nodes.label: prop:conv_one_to_one

nodes.statement: If \( (a_1, a_2), (a_1, a_3) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \), then there are \( i, j \) such that \( (i, a_1), (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2), (j, a_3) \in T_A^\Atom \). By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we deduce \( (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), so by coinjectivity of \( T_A^\Atom \), we deduce \( a_2 = a_3 \). Hence \( \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) is coinjective. By symmetry, \( \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) is one-to-one.
nodes.name: Proof of conv_one_to_one
nodes.statement_short: Coinjectivity from the atom condition of equal specifications; one-to-one by symmetry.
Unfold two pairs with the same source.
nodes.statement: If \( (a_1, a_2), (a_1, a_3) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \), then there are \( i, j \) such that \( (i, a_1), (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2), (j, a_3) \in T_A^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Unfold two pairs with the same source

nodes.statement_short: Equal specifications give a_2 = a_3, so coinjective.
nodes.statement: By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we deduce \( (j, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), so by coinjectivity of \( T_A^\Atom \), we deduce \( a_2 = a_3 \). Hence \( \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) is coinjective.
nodes.name: Equal specifications give a_2 = a_3, so coinjective

nodes.statement_short: Symmetric argument.
nodes.statement: By symmetry, \( \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) is one-to-one.
nodes.name: Symmetric argument

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). If \( (a_1, a_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \), then \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \).
nodes.name: conv_mem_nearLitter_iff
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \).
\( (a_1, a_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \) and \( (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \)
conclusions: \( a_1 \in N_1 \) if and only if \( a_2 \in N_2 \)
nodes.label: prop:conv_mem_nearLitter_iff

nodes.statement: As \( (a_1, a_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \), there is \( i \) such that \( (i, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), and as \( (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \), there is \( j \) such that \( (j, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (j, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \). By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we deduce that \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_1 \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_2 \in N) \] If \( a_1 \in N_1 \), then as \( (j, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \), we deduce that there is a near-litter \( N' \) such that \( (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \) and \( a \in N' \). But \( T_A^\NearLitter \) is coinjective, so \( N' = N_2 \), giving \( a \in N_2 \). The converse holds by symmetry.
nodes.name: Proof of conv_mem_nearLitter_iff
nodes.statement_short: Use the atom condition from equal specifications plus coinjectivity of the near-litter enumeration.
Unfold the indices i and j.
nodes.statement: As \( (a_1, a_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \), there is \( i \) such that \( (i, a_1) \in S_A^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2) \in T_A^\Atom \), and as \( (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \), there is \( j \) such that \( (j, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (j, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \).
nodes.name: Unfold the indices i and j

nodes.statement_short: The atom condition of equal specifications.
nodes.statement: By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we deduce that \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_1 \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge a_2 \in N) \]
nodes.name: The atom condition of equal specifications

nodes.statement_short: Forward direction via coinjectivity.
nodes.statement: If \( a_1 \in N_1 \), then as \( (j, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \), we deduce that there is a near-litter \( N' \) such that \( (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \) and \( a \in N' \). But \( T_A^\NearLitter \) is coinjective, so \( N' = N_2 \), giving \( a \in N_2 \).
nodes.name: Forward direction via coinjectivity

nodes.statement_short: Converse by symmetry.
nodes.statement: The converse holds by symmetry.
nodes.name: Converse by symmetry

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be supports such that \( T \) is strong and \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). If \( (N_1, N_3), (N_2, N_4) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \), then \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \) if and only if \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \).
nodes.name: conv_circ_eq_circ_iff
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be supports such that \( T \) is strong and \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \).
\( (N_1, N_3), (N_2, N_4) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \)
conclusions: \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \) if and only if \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \)
nodes.label: prop:conv_circ_eq_circ_iff

nodes.statement: There are \( i, j \) such that \( (i, N_1), (j, N_2) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_3), (j, N_4) \in T_A^\NearLitter \). Suppose that \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \); we show that \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \). First, suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible. Then by \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we have \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_1^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_3^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] So as \( (j, N_2) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \), there is \( N' \) with \( (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N_3^\circ = {N'}^\circ \), but clearly \( N' = N_4 \), giving the result. Now suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-inflexible, so there is an inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \) such that \[ A = {B_\varepsilon}_\bot;\quad N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \] Then by \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, there is some \( \delta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \( N_3^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \) and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} But as \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \), we draw the same conclusion about \( N_2 \) and \( N_4 \), giving a \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho' \) such that \( N_4^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho'(t)) \); note that the inflexible path and tangle in question will be the same for both pairs. We also have \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} Combining these, we obtain \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} We claim that \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \). As \( T \) is strong, for each atom \( a \) such that \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \), there is some \( k \) such that \( (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \). Thus \( \rho_B(a) = \rho'_B(a) \). The same conclusion may be drawn for near-litters. Thus \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \), giving \( \rho(t) = \rho'(t) \), and hence \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \).
nodes.name: Proof of conv_circ_eq_circ_iff
nodes.statement_short: Case split on flexibility of N_1; in the inflexible case compare the two permutations on supp(t) using strength of T.
Unfold indices.
nodes.statement: There are \( i, j \) such that \( (i, N_1), (j, N_2) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_3), (j, N_4) \in T_A^\NearLitter \).
nodes.name: Unfold indices

nodes.statement_short: Prove one direction.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \); we show that \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \).
nodes.name: Prove one direction

nodes.statement_short: Flexible: the flexible condition gives N_3, N_4 the same litter.
nodes.statement: First, suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible. Then by \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we have \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in S_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_1^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \wedge N_3^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] So as \( (j, N_2) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \), there is \( N' \) with \( (j, N') \in T_A^\NearLitter \) and \( N_3^\circ = {N'}^\circ \), but clearly \( N' = N_4 \), giving the result.
nodes.name: Flexible: the flexible condition gives N_3, N_4 the same litter

nodes.statement_short: Inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Now suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-inflexible, so there is an inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \) such that \[ A = {B_\varepsilon}_\bot;\quad N_1^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(t) \] Then by \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, there is some \( \delta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \( N_3^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \) and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} But as \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \), we draw the same conclusion about \( N_2 \) and \( N_4 \), giving a \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho' \) such that \( N_4^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho'(t)) \); note that the inflexible path and tangle in question will be the same for both pairs. We also have \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} Combining these, we obtain \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*} We claim that \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \). As \( T \) is strong, for each atom \( a \) such that \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \), there is some \( k \) such that \( (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \). Thus \( \rho_B(a) = \rho'_B(a) \). The same conclusion may be drawn for near-litters. Thus \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \), giving \( \rho(t) = \rho'(t) \), and hence \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \).
nodes.name: Inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: Get rho for N_3.
nodes.statement: Then by \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, there is some \( \delta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \( N_3^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \) and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*}
nodes.name: Get rho for N_3

nodes.statement_short: Get rho' for N_4.
nodes.statement: But as \( N_1^\circ = N_2^\circ \), we draw the same conclusion about \( N_2 \) and \( N_4 \), giving a \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho' \) such that \( N_4^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho'(t)) \); note that the inflexible path and tangle in question will be the same for both pairs. We also have \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*}
nodes.name: Get rho' for N_4

nodes.statement_short: Combine the two conditions.
nodes.statement: Combining these, we obtain \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_B^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, \rho_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho'_B(N)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\NearLitter \end{align*}
nodes.name: Combine the two conditions

nodes.statement_short: rho and rho' agree on supp(t).
nodes.statement: We claim that \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \). As \( T \) is strong, for each atom \( a \) such that \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \), there is some \( k \) such that \( (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \). Thus \( \rho_B(a) = \rho'_B(a) \). The same conclusion may be drawn for near-litters. Thus \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \), giving \( \rho(t) = \rho'(t) \), and hence \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \).
nodes.name: rho and rho' agree on supp(t)

nodes.statement_short: Strength of T makes them agree on atoms and near-litters.
nodes.statement: As \( T \) is strong, for each atom \( a \) such that \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_B^\Atom \), there is some \( k \) such that \( (i, \rho_B(a)) \in T_{{A_\delta}_B}^\Atom \). Thus \( \rho_B(a) = \rho'_B(a) \). The same conclusion may be drawn for near-litters.
nodes.name: Strength of T makes them agree on atoms and near-litters

nodes.statement_short: Hence rho(t) = rho'(t) and the litters agree.
nodes.statement: Thus \( \rho(\supp(t)) = \rho'(\supp(t)) \), giving \( \rho(t) = \rho'(t) \), and hence \( N_3^\circ = N_4^\circ \).
nodes.name: Hence rho(t) = rho'(t) and the litters agree

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be strong supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). Then for each \( (N_1, N_3), (N_2, N_4) \in \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter \), \[ \interf(N_1, N_2) \subseteq \coim \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom;\quad \interf(N_3, N_4) \subseteq \im \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom \]
nodes.name: conv_interf
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be strong supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \).
conclusions: \interf(N_1, N_2) \subseteq \coim \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom;\quad \interf(N_3, N_4) \subseteq \im \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom
nodes.label: prop:conv_interf

nodes.statement: As \( S \) is strong, we have \( \interf(N_1, N_2) \subseteq \im S_A^\Atom \). But \( \coim \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom = \im S_A^\Atom \), as required.\footnote{Make this a lemma.} The result for \( \interf(N_3, N_4) \) then follows by symmetry.
nodes.name: Proof of conv_interf
nodes.statement_short: Strength of S puts the interference in its atoms, which form the coimage; symmetric for T.

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be strong \( \beta \)-supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). Then for each \( A \), we define the base action \( \conv_{S_A, T_A} \) to be \( (\conv_{S_A, T_A}^\Atom, \conv_{S_A, T_A}^\NearLitter) \); this is a base action by \cref{prop:conv_one_to_one,prop:conv_mem_nearLitter_iff,prop:conv_circ_eq_circ_iff,prop:conv_interf}. We now define the \( \beta \)-action \( \conv_{S,T} \) by \( (\conv_{S,T})_A = \conv_{S_A,T_A} \).
nodes.name: conversion action
nodes.label: def:conv

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be strong supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). Then \( \conv_{S,T} \) is coherent.
nodes.name: conv_coherent
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be strong supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \).
conclusions: \( \conv_{S,T} \) is coherent
nodes.label: prop:conv_coherent

nodes.statement: Suppose that \( (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S_A,T_A}^\NearLitter \), so there is \( i \) such that \( (i, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \). Suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible. By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we immediately conclude that \( N_2^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible as required. Now suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( N_2^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \) and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_C(a)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_C^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_C(N)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\NearLitter \end{align*} We must show that \( ((\conv_{S,T})_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \). We will show the result for atoms; the result for near-litters is identical. Let \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom \). Then as \( S \) is strong, there is \( k \) such that \( (k, a) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \). Then by the equation above, \( (k, \rho_C(a)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \). Hence \( (a, \rho_C(a)) \in (((\conv_{S,T})_B)_\delta)_C \) as required.
nodes.name: Proof of conv_coherent
nodes.statement_short: Flexible case from equal specifications; inflexible case shows the conversion action agrees with the witnessing permutation on supp(t) using strength.
Unfold a near-litter pair.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( (N_1, N_2) \in \conv_{S_A,T_A}^\NearLitter \), so there is \( i \) such that \( (i, N_1) \in S_A^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_A^\NearLitter \).
nodes.name: Unfold a near-litter pair

nodes.statement_short: Flexible case is immediate.
nodes.statement: Suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible. By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, we immediately conclude that \( N_2^\circ \) is \( A \)-flexible as required.
nodes.name: Flexible case is immediate

nodes.statement_short: Inflexible case.
nodes.statement: Now suppose that \( N_1^\circ \) is \( A \)-inflexible with inflexible \( \beta \)-path \( I = (\gamma,\delta,\varepsilon,B) \) and tangle \( t : \Tang_\delta \). By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( N_2^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \) and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_C(a)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_C^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_C(N)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\NearLitter \end{align*} We must show that \( ((\conv_{S,T})_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \). We will show the result for atoms; the result for near-litters is identical. Let \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom \). Then as \( S \) is strong, there is \( k \) such that \( (k, a) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \). Then by the equation above, \( (k, \rho_C(a)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \). Hence \( (a, \rho_C(a)) \in (((\conv_{S,T})_B)_\delta)_C \) as required.
nodes.name: Inflexible case

nodes.statement_short: Get the witness rho.
nodes.statement: By \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff}, there is some \( \delta \)-allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( N_2^\circ = f_{\delta,\varepsilon}(\rho(t)) \) and \begin{align*} \forall j,\, \forall a,\, (j, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom &\to \forall i,\, (i, a) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_C(a)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \\ \forall j,\, \forall N,\, (j, N) \in \supp(t)_C^\NearLitter &\to \forall i,\, (i, N) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\NearLitter \leftrightarrow (i, \rho_C(N)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\NearLitter \end{align*}
nodes.name: Get the witness rho

nodes.statement_short: Target: agreement on supp(t), atoms only.
nodes.statement: We must show that \( ((\conv_{S,T})_B)_\delta(\supp(t)) = \rho(\supp(t)) \). We will show the result for atoms; the result for near-litters is identical.
nodes.name: Target: agreement on supp(t), atoms only

nodes.statement_short: Strength of S indexes a in S.
nodes.statement: Let \( (j, a) \in \supp(t)_C^\Atom \). Then as \( S \) is strong, there is \( k \) such that \( (k, a) \in S_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \).
nodes.name: Strength of S indexes a in S

nodes.statement_short: So a maps to rho_C(a).
nodes.statement: Then by the equation above, \( (k, \rho_C(a)) \in T_{{B_\delta}_C}^\Atom \). Hence \( (a, \rho_C(a)) \in (((\conv_{S,T})_B)_\delta)_C \) as required.
nodes.name: So a maps to rho_C(a)

nodes.statement: Let \( S, T \) be strong supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \). Then there is an allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( \rho(S) = T \).
nodes.name: exists_allowable_of_spec_eq_spec
assumptions: Let \( S, T \) be strong supports such that \( \spec(S) = \spec(T) \).
conclusions: there is an allowable permutation \( \rho \) such that \( \rho(S) = T \)
nodes.label: prop:exists_allowable_of_spec_eq_spec

nodes.statement: By \cref{prop:conv_coherent}, we may apply \cref{thm:StrAction.foa} to \( \conv_{S,T} \) to obtain an allowable permutation \( \rho \) that \( \conv_{S,T} \) approximates, which directly gives \( \rho(S) = T \) as required.
nodes.name: Proof of exists_allowable_of_spec_eq_spec
nodes.statement_short: Apply freedom of action for actions to the coherent conversion action.

nodes.statement: Let \( \gamma < \beta \) be proper type indices at most \( \alpha \). An object \( x : \TSet_\beta \) is called a \emph{\( \gamma \)-combination} of a set of \( \beta \)-coding functions \( s \) with respect to a \( \beta \)-support \( S \) if \[ U_\beta(x)(\gamma) = \bigcup_{(V, v) \in \chi \in s,\, V \geq S} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) \] By extensionality, a set of coding functions \( s \) has at most one \( \gamma \)-combination with respect to a given support \( S \).
nodes.name: gamma-combination
nodes.label: def:Combination

nodes.statement: If \( x \) is a \( \gamma \)-combination of \( s \) with respect to \( S \) then \( \rho(x) \) is a \( \gamma \)-combination of \( s \) with respect to \( \rho(S) \).
nodes.name: Combination.smul
assumptions: \( x \) is a \( \gamma \)-combination of \( s \) with respect to \( S \)
conclusions: \( \rho(x) \) is a \( \gamma \)-combination of \( s \) with respect to \( \rho(S) \)
nodes.label: prop:Combination.smul

nodes.statement: We can calculate \begin{align*} U_\beta(\rho(x))(\gamma) &= \rho_\gamma[U_\beta(x)(\gamma)] \\ &= \rho_\gamma\left[ \bigcup_{(V, v) \in \chi \in s,\, V \geq S} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) \right] \\ &= \bigcup_{(V, v) \in \chi \in s,\, V \geq S} \rho_\gamma\left[ U_\beta(v)(\gamma) \right] \\ &= \bigcup_{(V, v) \in \chi \in s,\, V \geq S} U_\beta(\rho(v))(\gamma) \\ &= \bigcup_{(V, v) \in \chi \in s,\, V \geq \rho(S)} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) \end{align*} where the last inequality uses the fact that coding functions are defined on a support orbit.
nodes.name: Proof of Combination.smul
nodes.statement_short: Direct calculation pushing rho through the union.

nodes.statement: Let \( s \) be a set of \( \beta \)-coding functions, and let \( o \) be a \( \beta \)-support orbit such that for each \( S \in o \), \( s \) has a \( \gamma \)-combination \( x \) with respect to \( S \) where \( S \) supports \( x \). Then the \emph{\( (\gamma,\beta) \)-raised coding function} for \( (s, o) \) is the relation \( \chi : \StrSupp_\beta \to \TSet_\beta \to \Prop \) defined by the constructor \[ \forall S \in o,\, \forall x \text{ combinations of } (s, S),\, (S, x) \in \chi \]
nodes.name: raised coding function
nodes.label: def:raisedCodingFunction

nodes.statement: The \( (\gamma,\beta) \)-raised coding function for \( (s, o) \) is a coding function.
nodes.name: raisedCodingFunction_spec
conclusions: The \( (\gamma,\beta) \)-raised coding function for \( (s, o) \) is a coding function.
nodes.label: prop:raisedCodingFunction_spec

nodes.statement: Coinjectivity follows from uniqueness of combinations. The nonemptiness and support orbit conditions follow from the definition, as does the condition that \( (S, x) \in \chi \) implies that \( S \) is a support for \( x \). It remains to show that if \( (S, x) \in \chi \) and \( \rho \) is \( \beta \)-allowable, then \( (\rho(S), \rho(x)) \in \chi \), and this follows directly from \cref{prop:Combination.smul}.
nodes.name: Proof of raisedCodingFunction_spec
nodes.statement_short: Check each coding-function axiom; equivariance from Combination.smul.
Coinjectivity from uniqueness of combinations.
nodes.statement: Coinjectivity follows from uniqueness of combinations.
nodes.name: Coinjectivity from uniqueness of combinations

nodes.statement_short: Other conditions from the definition.
nodes.statement: The nonemptiness and support orbit conditions follow from the definition, as does the condition that \( (S, x) \in \chi \) implies that \( S \) is a support for \( x \).
nodes.name: Other conditions from the definition

nodes.statement_short: Equivariance via Combination.smul.
nodes.statement: It remains to show that if \( (S, x) \in \chi \) and \( \rho \) is \( \beta \)-allowable, then \( (\rho(S), \rho(x)) \in \chi \), and this follows directly from \cref{prop:Combination.smul}.
nodes.name: Equivariance via Combination.smul

nodes.statement: For a type index \( \beta \leq \alpha \), a \emph{\( \beta \)-set orbit} is the quotient of \( \TSet_\beta \) under the relation of being in the same orbit under \( \beta \)-allowable permutations. We write \( [x] \) for the set orbit of \( x \). For each set orbit \( o \), we choose a representative \( \repr(o) : \TSet_\beta \) with \( [\repr(o)] = o \), and define a support \( S_o \) for \( \repr(o) \). For each set, we choose a \( \beta \)-allowable permutation \( \twist_t \) with the property that \( \twist_t(\repr([t])) = t \), and we define the \emph{designated support} of \( t \) to be \( \dsupp(t) = \twist_t(S_{[t]}) \). This is a support for \( t \).
nodes.name: designated support
nodes.label: def:designatedSupport

nodes.statement: Let \( \gamma < \beta \) be proper type indices. Let \( S \) be a \( \beta \)-support and let \( u : \TSet_\gamma \). Then the \emph{\( (\gamma,\beta ) \)-raised singleton} coding function is \[ \rsing(S, u) = \chi_{(\singleton_\beta(u), S + \dsupp(u)^\beta)} \] A coding function is called a \emph{\( (\gamma,\beta) \)-raised singleton} if it is of the form \( \rsing(S, u) \).
nodes.name: raised singleton
nodes.label: def:raisedSingleton

nodes.statement: Let \( \gamma < \beta \) be proper type indices, and let \( x : \TSet_\beta \). Then for any support \( S \) of \( x \), \( x \) is a combination of the set \[ \{ \rsing(S, u) \mid u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \} \]
nodes.name: raise_combination
assumptions: Let \( \gamma < \beta \) be proper type indices, and let \( x : \TSet_\beta \).
conclusions: for any support \( S \) of \( x \), \( x \) is a combination of the set \[ \{ \rsing(S, u) \mid u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \} \]
nodes.label: prop:raise_combination

nodes.statement: We must show that \[ U_\beta(x)(\gamma) = \bigcup_{u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma),\,(V,v) \in \rsing(S, u),\, V \geq S} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) \] First, suppose \( u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \). Then we have \[ (S + \dsupp(u)^\beta, \singleton_\beta(u)) \in \rsing(S, u);\quad u \in U_\beta(\singleton_\beta(u))(\gamma) \] so the left-hand side is contained in the right-hand side. For the converse, suppose that \( u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \) and \( (V, v) \in \rsing(S, u) \) with \( V \geq S \). As \( (V, v) \in \rsing(S, u) \), there is some \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \[ \rho(S + \dsupp(u)^\beta) = V;\quad \rho(\singleton_\beta(u)) = v \] As \( V \geq S \), we obtain \( \rho(S) = S \),\footnote{This is a good lemma.} so \( \rho(x) = x \). Then \begin{align*} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) &= U_\beta(\rho(\singleton_\beta(u)))(\gamma) \\ &= U_\beta(\singleton_\beta(\rho_\gamma(u)))(\gamma) \\ &= \{ \rho_\gamma(u) \} \\ &\subseteq U_\beta(\rho(x))(\gamma) \\ &= U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \end{align*} as required.
nodes.name: Proof of raise_combination
nodes.statement_short: Double inclusion: singletons give the forward inclusion; for the converse a permutation fixing S fixes x.
State the target equality.
nodes.statement: We must show that \[ U_\beta(x)(\gamma) = \bigcup_{u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma),\,(V,v) \in \rsing(S, u),\, V \geq S} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) \]
nodes.name: State the target equality

nodes.statement_short: Each u lies in its own raised singleton.
nodes.statement: First, suppose \( u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \). Then we have \[ (S + \dsupp(u)^\beta, \singleton_\beta(u)) \in \rsing(S, u);\quad u \in U_\beta(\singleton_\beta(u))(\gamma) \] so the left-hand side is contained in the right-hand side.
nodes.name: Each u lies in its own raised singleton

nodes.statement_short: Converse inclusion.
nodes.statement: For the converse, suppose that \( u \in U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \) and \( (V, v) \in \rsing(S, u) \) with \( V \geq S \). As \( (V, v) \in \rsing(S, u) \), there is some \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \[ \rho(S + \dsupp(u)^\beta) = V;\quad \rho(\singleton_\beta(u)) = v \] As \( V \geq S \), we obtain \( \rho(S) = S \),\footnote{This is a good lemma.} so \( \rho(x) = x \). Then \begin{align*} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) &= U_\beta(\rho(\singleton_\beta(u)))(\gamma) \\ &= U_\beta(\singleton_\beta(\rho_\gamma(u)))(\gamma) \\ &= \{ \rho_\gamma(u) \} \\ &\subseteq U_\beta(\rho(x))(\gamma) \\ &= U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \end{align*} as required.
nodes.name: Converse inclusion

nodes.statement_short: Get rho mapping the support and singleton.
nodes.statement: As \( (V, v) \in \rsing(S, u) \), there is some \( \beta \)-allowable \( \rho \) such that \[ \rho(S + \dsupp(u)^\beta) = V;\quad \rho(\singleton_\beta(u)) = v \]
nodes.name: Get rho mapping the support and singleton

nodes.statement_short: rho fixes S and hence x.
nodes.statement: As \( V \geq S \), we obtain \( \rho(S) = S \),\footnote{This is a good lemma.} so \( \rho(x) = x \).
nodes.name: rho fixes S and hence x

nodes.statement_short: Compute U(v)(gamma) inside U(x)(gamma).
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} U_\beta(v)(\gamma) &= U_\beta(\rho(\singleton_\beta(u)))(\gamma) \\ &= U_\beta(\singleton_\beta(\rho_\gamma(u)))(\gamma) \\ &= \{ \rho_\gamma(u) \} \\ &\subseteq U_\beta(\rho(x))(\gamma) \\ &= U_\beta(x)(\gamma) \end{align*} as required.

nodes.statement: Let \( \gamma < \beta \) be proper type indices, and let \( \chi \) be a \( \beta \)-coding function. nodes.statement: Let \( i \) be an index that does not occur in \( \coim S^\Atom \), and define \( T_1, T_2 \) by \[ U_n^\Atom = S^\Atom \sqcup \{ (i, a_n) \};\quad U_n^\NearLitter = S^\NearLitter \] for \( n = 1, 2 \). We claim that \( T_1 \) and \( T_2 \) are have the same specification, treated as \( \bot \)-supports. By appealing to \cref{prop:spec_eq_spec_iff} and noting that every litter is flexible for the unique path \( \bot \tpath \bot \), it suffices to check: \begin{itemize} \item (atom condition) For all \( i, a_1, a_2 \), if \( (i, a_1) \in T_1^\Atom \) and \( (i, a_2) \in T_2^\Atom \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (j, a_1) \in T_1^\Atom \leftrightarrow (j, a_2) \in T_2^\Atom \] and \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_1^\NearLitter \wedge a_1 \in N) \leftrightarrow (\exists N,\, (j, N) \in T_2^\NearLitter \wedge a_2 \in N) \] \item (litter condition) For all \( i, N_1, N_2 \), if \( (i, N_1) \in T_1^\NearLitter \) and \( (i, N_2) \in T_2^\NearLitter \), we have \[ \forall j,\, (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_1^\NearLitter \wedge N_1^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \leftrightarrow (\exists N',\, (j, N') \in T_2^\NearLitter \wedge N_2^\circ = {N'}^\circ) \] \end{itemize} The atom condition follows directly from the two assumptions, and the litter condition is vacuously true as \( T_1^\NearLitter = T_2^\NearLitter \). Note also that \( T_1, T_2 \) are strong, treated as \( \bot \)-supports. Then, by \cref{prop:exists_allowable_of_spec_eq_spec}, there is a \( \bot \)-allowable permutation \( \pi \) such that \( \pi(T_1) = T_2 \). Thus, \( \pi(S) = S \) and \( \pi(a_1) = a_2 \).

nodes.statement: Suppose that for all type indices \( \delta < \beta \), there are strictly less than \( \#\mu \)-many \( \delta \)-coding functions. Then there are less than \( \#\mu \) \( \beta \)-specifications.
nodes.name: card_spec
assumptions: Suppose that for all type indices \( \delta < \beta \), there are strictly less than \( \#\mu \)-many \( \delta \)-coding functions.
conclusions: there are less than \( \#\mu \) \( \beta \)-specifications
nodes.label: prop:card_spec

nodes.statement: There are less than \( \#\mu \) atom conditions as \( \#\kappa < \#\mu \) and \( \#\mu \) is a strong limit. There are less than \( \#\mu \) inflexible \( \beta \)-paths, as each is determined by three type indices less than \( \beta \) and a path with maximum less than \( \beta \), of which there are \( \#\mu \)-many. There are less than \( \#\mu \)-many coding functions of any type \( \delta < \beta \), because K\"onig's theorem gives \[ \sum_{\delta < \beta} \#\{\delta\text{-coding functions}\} < \prod_{\delta < \beta} \#\mu = \#\mu^{\#\{\delta < \beta\}} = \#\mu \] where the last equality follows from the facts that \( \#\{\delta < \beta\} \) has cardinality less than \( \cof(\ord(\#\mu)) \) and that \( \#\mu \) is a strong limit. There are less than \( \#\mu \) \( \delta \)-trees of relations on \( \kappa \) for each \( \delta \leq \alpha \), because there are less than \( \#\mu \)-many relations on \( \kappa \) as \( \#\mu \) is a strong limit, allowing us to conclude by one of the remarks in \cref{def:Tree}. Hence there are less than \( \#\mu \) \( \beta \)-near-litter conditions. We can again apply the result about cardinalities of types of trees to deduce that there are less than \( \#\mu \) \( \beta \)-trees of enumerations of atom conditions and of \( \beta \)-near-litter conditions, as required.
nodes.name: Proof of card_spec
